title: The Marvelous Land of Oz
author: L. Frank Baum
summary: Oz book 2 of 14. A chapter-by-chapter title following Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead and the Scarecrow as they try to win back the Emerald City. Pass each chapter as you read it, then sit the whole-book test at the end.

questions.q: In which part of the Land of Oz does Tip live?
options: The Country of the Gillikins, in the North
questions.why: The chapter opens by placing Tip in the Country of the Gillikins, in the North of Oz.

questions.q: How did Tip come to live with old Mombi?
options: He wandered to her farm after a cyclone
Mombi is his grandmother, who raised him after his parents moved away
He answered her notice asking for a farm helper
He was carried to her as a small child to be brought up, and he remembers nothing of his parents
questions.why: The text says Tip was brought to Mombi when very small and could not remember his parents.

questions.q: Why do the Gillikin people distrust Mombi?
options: She refuses to sell them her corn
She once tried to become their queen
They suspect she practices magical arts
She keeps a dangerous four-horned cow loose on the roads
questions.why: Mombi's reputation is poor because people believe she works magic.

questions.q: Why does the story say Mombi was not openly called a Witch?
options: Mombi had given up all magic long ago
The Good Witch who ruled that part of the land did not allow any other witch there
Only people born in the Emerald City could be witches
The Wizard of Oz had taken away her powers
questions.why: The chapter explains that the Good Witch of the North forbade other witches, so Mombi was more of a sorceress.

questions.q: Which of these was one of Tip's chores for Mombi?
options: Selling eggs in the Emerald City
questions.why: Tip's duties included carrying wood, working in the corn, feeding the pigs, and milking the four-horned cow.

questions.q: What does the chapter suggest about how Tip treated his chores?
options: He finished every job before sunrise
He paid other children to do them
He refused to do any work at all
He often slipped away from work to have fun instead
questions.why: Instead of gathering wood, Tip would climb trees for birds' eggs, chase rabbits, or fish with bent pins.

questions.q: How did Tip feel about Mombi?
options: He loved her like a mother
He was too frightened to have any opinion of her
He disliked her and did not try very hard to hide it
He admired her magic and wanted to learn it
questions.why: The chapter states plainly that Tip did not like Mombi and did not try to hide his feelings.

questions.q: What did Tip use to make Jack's head?
options: A big pumpkin with a bright orange-red color
A large turnip from the garden
questions.why: Tip chose a fine, big pumpkin with a lustrous orange-red color.

questions.q: Which face did Tip carve into the pumpkin?
options: Two round eyes, a three-cornered nose, and a mouth shaped like a new moon
Two square eyes, a round nose, and a frowning mouth
One big eye in the middle and a crooked mouth
Star-shaped eyes and a mouth full of pointed teeth
questions.why: The text describes the eyes, three-cornered nose, and new-moon mouth exactly this way.

questions.q: The pumpkin face was so 'jolly' that even Tip laughed. What does 'jolly' mean here?
questions.why: A jolly face is a happy, merry one, which is why Tip laughed at it.

questions.q: What did Tip use to make Jack's arms and legs?
options: Old broom handles from the house
Stout, straight saplings he cut in the forest
questions.why: Tip went to the forest, cut straight young trees, and trimmed them for limbs.

questions.q: How did Tip make Jack's body?
options: He used an empty pickle barrel
He shaped a thick sheet of tree bark into a cylinder and pinned it with wooden pegs
He stuffed one of Mombi's old dresses with straw
He carved it from a single log
questions.why: The body was a cylinder of bark whose edges Tip pinned together with wooden pegs.

questions.q: What had Tip forgotten when he first put the man together, and when did he fix it?
options: A neck; he made one from wood the next morning
The feet; he carved them that same night
The ears; he never made any
The hands; Mombi made them later
questions.why: Tip realized he had no neck to hold the head and cut wood for it the next morning.

questions.q: Where did Tip find the clothes for his pumpkin man?
options: On a scarecrow in the field
In a trunk left by a traveler
questions.why: Tip ransacked Mombi's chest of old things to dress the figure.

questions.q: Which outfit did Tip put on the pumpkin man?
options: A green coat and yellow boots
A blue suit with a tall hat
Purple trousers, a red shirt, and a pink vest with white spots
A white robe and a gold crown
questions.why: The text lists purple trousers, a red shirt, and a pink vest dotted with white spots.

questions.q: What did the pumpkin man wear on his feet?
options: Knit stockings of Mombi's and a well-worn pair of Tip's own shoes
questions.why: Tip added Mombi's knit stockings and an old pair of his own shoes.

questions.q: What name did Tip give his creation?
questions.why: Tip declares he will name the fellow 'Jack Pumpkinhead.'

questions.q: What was Tip's main reason for building the pumpkin man?
options: To scare crows away from the corn
To have a friend to talk to
To sell at the village market
To frighten Mombi as a prank
questions.why: Tip planned to place the figure where Mombi would meet it face to face and be scared.

questions.q: Why was this a good time for Tip to work on his project without being caught?
options: It was night and Mombi was asleep
Mombi had gone off on a trip of at least two days to a village for groceries
Mombi had gone to visit the Scarecrow
questions.why: Mombi's trip to the village gave Tip time to build the figure undisturbed.

questions.q: What does the way Tip builds Jack show about Tip?
options: He is lazy about every kind of task
He is clever and willing to work hard on something he chooses to do
He is afraid of the forest
He does not know how to use a knife
questions.why: Though he shirked chores, Tip labored carefully with his knife, bark, and pegs to build Jack.

questions.q: Where did Tip decide to put Jack Pumpkinhead?
options: At the bend in the road, a little way from the house
On the roof of the farmhouse
In the middle of the corn field
questions.why: The chapter begins with Tip choosing the bend in the road near the house.

questions.q: What problem did Tip fix while moving Jack to the road?
options: Jack's left arm had fallen off, so Tip made a stronger pin for it
Jack's pumpkin head split in two
Jack's shoes were lost in the mud
questions.why: Tip found the fallen arm and fastened it with a stouter peg.

questions.q: What did Tip do while he waited for Mombi to come home?
options: He took a nap in the barn
He walked to the Emerald City
He went to the valley below the farmhouse to gather nuts
questions.why: Tip went nutting in the valley while waiting for Mombi.

questions.q: Why was Mombi in a hurry to get home?
options: She was afraid of a storm
She had left her kettle on the fire
She wanted to try out the new magic she had gotten from a crooked wizard
She wanted to punish Tip for skipping chores
questions.why: Mombi had traded secrets with a crooked wizard and was eager to test what she got.

questions.q: What did Mombi get from the crooked wizard?
options: A magic wand and a flying broom
Three new recipes, four magical powders, and a selection of herbs
A golden cap and silver shoes
questions.why: The text lists three recipes, four powders, and herbs.

questions.q: How did Mombi first react when she saw Jack by the road?
options: She spoke politely to him, then realized it was Tip's trick and was about to smash it
She screamed and ran all the way home
She laughed and walked past without stopping
questions.why: Mombi began with a polite greeting, then recognized the pumpkin and raised her stick to break it.

questions.q: Why did Mombi stop herself from destroying the pumpkin man?
options: She thought it would make a good scarecrow
Tip begged her to spare it
She decided to use him to test whether the wizard's powder really worked
questions.why: Mombi paused, thinking it a good chance to see if the wizard had cheated her.

questions.q: In what kind of container was the Powder of Life kept?
questions.why: Mombi took from her basket an old pepper-box labeled 'Powder of Life.'

questions.q: How much powder did Mombi say the wizard had given her?
options: Enough to bring an army to life
Not much, but enough for two or three doses
questions.why: Mombi grumbled the wizard gave little, but enough for two or three doses.

questions.q: The narrator says Mombi sprinkled the powder the way someone would pepper a baked potato. What does this comparison show?
options: She shook it lightly over the top of Jack's head
She poured it into Jack's mouth
She mixed it into water first
She rubbed it hard into Jack's shoes
questions.why: Peppering a potato means shaking a fine powder lightly over it.

questions.q: Where was Tip while Mombi worked the magic?
options: Up in a tall tree far away
questions.why: Tip came back with nuts, saw Mombi, and hid behind a hedge to watch.

questions.q: Which set of words did Mombi say, in order, as she made her gestures?
questions.why: Mombi said Weaugh (left little finger up), Teaugh (right thumb up), then Peaugh (both hands spread).

questions.q: What were Jack Pumpkinhead's very first words?
options: "Don't yell like that! Do you think I'm deaf?"
questions.why: Jack stepped back and complained about Mombi's shouting.

questions.q: How did Mombi react when Jack came to life?
options: She danced and shouted, "He lives! he lives! he lives!"
She burst into tears of fear
She quietly wrote notes on a paper
She ran to tell the Scarecrow
questions.why: Mombi screamed with delight and danced about, hugging herself.

questions.q: Why did Tip start laughing while watching?
options: Mombi tripped and fell in the mud
Jack's carved, jolly face looked so droll and comical
questions.why: After his fright passed, Tip found Jack's comical expression funny.

questions.q: After Mombi caught Tip, what did she tell him to do on the way home?
options: Run ahead and light a fire
Stay behind and guard the road
questions.why: Mombi said they must get home before dark and told Tip to help Jack walk, though Jack said he could walk himself.

questions.q: Where did Mombi put Jack when they reached the farm?
options: In a cage in the kitchen
In an empty stall in the cow stable, with the door fastened
Back at the bend in the road
questions.why: Mombi shut Jack up in an empty stall of the cow stable.

questions.q: When Mombi says "You won't be hungry long," what is she really hinting?
options: She plans to change Tip into something that will not need food
She is about to cook him a big dinner
She will send him to the village to eat
She thinks nuts will fill him up
questions.why: Right after, she brews a potion to turn Tip into a marble statue, which would never be hungry.

questions.q: What did Mombi say the potion in the black kettle would do to Tip?
options: Transform him into a marble statue
questions.why: Mombi said that, if properly made, it would change him into a marble statue.

questions.q: Why did Mombi want Tip to become a statue?
options: To sell him to the Emerald City
To protect the farm from robbers
To use him as an ornament in her spring flower garden, since he had been a bother to her for years
To keep him safe from the Wizard
questions.why: Mombi said she would put him in the middle of her flower garden and complained he had been a bother.

questions.q: What did Tip decide to do rather than drink the potion?
options: Pour the potion out and stay
Ask the Good Witch for help
Run away before Mombi could make him drink it
Drink it and hope it failed
questions.why: Tip thought being a statue would be hard and decided to run away first.

questions.q: How did Tip know it was safe to begin his escape?
options: Mombi told him she was leaving
Jack signaled him from the stable
questions.why: Tip waited until Mombi's snores showed she was asleep.

questions.q: What food did Tip take for his journey?
options: Only the nuts in his pocket
questions.why: He found crusts of bread on the shelf and cheese in Mombi's basket.

questions.q: Why did Tip take the pepper-box of Powder of Life?
options: Because he wanted to become a wizard
So Mombi could not use it to make more mischief
questions.why: Tip thought he might as well take it, or Mombi would use it for mischief.

questions.q: What was the word 'fugitives' in the chapter title most likely describing?
options: People who are lost at sea
questions.why: The chapter is about Tip and Jack fleeing Mombi, and fugitives are people who flee.

questions.q: Why did Tip go back for Jack instead of leaving alone?
options: He needed Jack to carry the food
He felt Jack belonged to him because he made him, and did not want to leave him to Mombi
Mombi ordered him to take Jack
He was afraid to travel at night alone
questions.why: Tip reasoned that Jack was his since he made him, and did not want to leave him to Mombi's mercy.

questions.q: When Jack asked 'Where to?', what did Tip answer?
options: "You'll know as soon as I do."
questions.why: Tip answered that Jack would know as soon as he did, since Tip had no plan yet.

questions.q: How did Jack walk at first?
options: He could not walk and had to be carried
Awkwardly, sometimes stumbling when a leg joint turned the wrong way
questions.why: Jack limped and stumbled when his joints turned backward, then learned to step carefully.

questions.q: Why did Tip take several different paths during the night?
options: To find a place to buy food
To confuse anyone who might try to follow them
Because Jack wanted to see the sights
questions.why: Tip changed paths so pursuers would have trouble tracking them.

questions.q: Why did Jack refuse to eat breakfast?
options: He said he did not seem to be made the same way Tip was
questions.why: Jack watched Tip eat and said he was not made the same way.

questions.q: What did Jack conclude after Tip said he had made Jack's body and face?
options: That Tip must be his creator, his parent, his father
That Tip was a great wizard
That he was a real pumpkin
questions.why: Jack exclaimed that Tip must be his creator, parent, and father.

questions.q: How did Tip respond to being called Jack's father?
options: He was angry and told Jack to leave
He proudly agreed and hugged Jack
He said Mombi was the real parent
He laughed and called himself Jack's inventor instead
questions.why: Tip laughed and said he was more of an inventor.

questions.q: What 'deal' did Jack describe between himself and Tip?
options: Jack will pay Tip in gold
Tip must build Jack a house
Jack owes Tip obedience, and Tip owes Jack support
They will take turns being in charge
questions.why: Jack said he must obey Tip and Tip must support him, and Tip agreed.

questions.q: In which direction were Tip and Jack heading, and to where?
questions.why: Tip said they were going South to the Emerald City.

questions.q: According to Tip, what is the favorite color of the Gillikin Country?
questions.why: Tip explains that in the Gillikin Country the grass, trees, and houses are purple.

questions.q: Which pairing of country and color is correct, according to Tip?
questions.why: Tip lists Munchkins blue, Quadlings red, Winkies yellow, and the Emerald City green.

questions.q: Who does Tip say rules the Winkies?
questions.why: Tip says the Tin Woodman rules the Winkie Country.

questions.q: According to Tip, how did the Wizard leave the Emerald City?
options: He was carried off by a cyclone
He made a big balloon and escaped in it
He rode away on a flying horse
He turned himself into a bird
questions.why: Tip says the Wizard made a balloon, escaped, and was never seen again.

questions.q: Jack says he understands the history 'perfectly — all but the explanation.' What does this line show?
options: Jack is confused but does not realize how confused he is, which makes it funny
Jack is the smartest character in the story
Jack does not want to hear any more
Jack already knew all about Oz
questions.why: Jack claims to understand everything except the explanation itself, a humorous sign of his confusion.

questions.q: Who became the ruler of the Emerald City after the Wizard left?
options: The Wicked Witch of the West
The Scarecrow, who became a very popular ruler
questions.why: Tip explains that the people made the Scarecrow their King.

chapters.title: 4. Tip Makes an Experiment in Magic

questions.q: How did Tip feel about being called 'father' by Jack?
options: Angry, so he made Jack stop
Confused, so he asked Mombi about it
Awkward, but he decided not to explain further
questions.why: Tip, a small boy being called father by a tall man, felt awkward but let it go.

questions.q: What worry did Jack have when Tip asked if he was tired?
options: That his pumpkin head would rot
That his wooden joints would wear out from walking
questions.why: Jack said he was not tired but feared his joints would wear out.

questions.q: What did Tip regret about how he built Jack?
options: That he used a pumpkin for the head
That he had not made the joints more carefully
That he gave Jack a smile
questions.why: Tip wished he had built stronger joints, not expecting Jack would come to life.

questions.q: Where did Tip and Jack stop to rest?
options: At the edge of a wood, where an old sawhorse had been left
Beside the gates of the Emerald City
On a bridge over a river
questions.why: They reached the edge of a wood and Tip sat on a sawhorse a woodcutter had left.

questions.q: What happened when Jack tried to sit down?
options: He sat perfectly and fell asleep
His head rolled into the woods
His joints gave way and he crashed to the ground
questions.why: Jack's joints gave way completely and he fell.

questions.q: What advice did Tip give Jack after helping him up?
options: That he should lie down whenever possible
That he should sit only on soft grass
That he had better stay standing from then on
That he should crawl instead of walk
questions.why: Tip said Jack had better remain standing hereafter.

questions.q: What was Tip sitting on, and what was it used for?
options: A tree stump used as a table
A wooden sawhorse used for sawing logs
questions.why: Tip explained it was a wooden horse used to saw logs upon.

questions.q: How did Jack reason that the sawhorse was a horse?
options: It had four legs, a head, and a tail, just like Tip's description
Tip said it could run fast
It was brown like a horse
questions.why: Jack pointed out the sawhorse fit Tip's description of four legs, head, and tail.

questions.q: Which part of the sawhorse looked like a tail?
options: A branch sticking out of the log body
questions.why: Tip noticed a branch on the trunk-body that resembled a tail.

questions.q: What looked like the sawhorse's eyes?
questions.why: Tip saw knots in the wood that looked like eyes.

questions.q: Tip said the sawhorse could not be alive because it was wooden. What did Jack reply?
questions.why: Jack pointed out that he too was wooden, yet alive.

questions.q: What gave Tip the idea to bring the sawhorse to life?
options: Jack's remark reminded him he still had the Powder of Life in his pocket
He found a spell book in the woods
questions.why: After Jack said 'So am I,' Tip remembered the powder in his pocket.

questions.q: Why did Jack like the idea of a living sawhorse?
options: He wanted a pet to play with
He hoped it would carry food
He could ride it and save his joints from wearing out
questions.why: Jack calmly said he could ride it and save his joints.

questions.q: How did Tip know the magic words and gestures?
options: They were written on the pepper-box
He had watched Mombi closely from behind the hedge
questions.why: Tip recalled watching Mombi carefully from the hedge.

questions.q: When Jack asked what 'Weaugh!' meant, what did Tip say?
questions.why: Tip admitted he did not know what the word meant.

questions.q: When Jack asked what 'Teaugh!' meant, Tip said it meant Jack must keep quiet. Why did Tip say this?
options: He was annoyed at being interrupted during the spell
That was truly the meaning of the word
He was trying to scare the sawhorse
questions.why: Tip answered irritably because Jack's questions interrupted him; he did not know the real meaning.

questions.q: How did Jack respond to Tip's snappy answer?
options: He said contentedly, "How fast I am learning!"
questions.why: Jack took Tip's words as a lesson and was pleased.

questions.q: What gesture went with the final word, 'Peaugh!'?
options: Both hands raised above the head with fingers and thumbs spread
questions.why: Tip lifted both hands with all fingers and thumbs spread and cried Peaugh.

questions.q: What did the sawhorse do right after the spell?
options: It ran straight into the woods
It stretched its legs, yawned, and shook the powder off its back
questions.why: The sawhorse moved, stretched, yawned with its chopped mouth, and shook off the powder.

questions.q: What does this chapter suggest about Tip?
options: He is curious and bold enough to try magic himself
He is afraid of anything magical
He wants to be just like Mombi in every way
questions.why: Tip decides to experiment with the powder and carefully copies the spell.

questions.q: Why couldn't the Saw-horse look at its own body?
options: It had no neck to turn its head
questions.why: The Saw-horse rolled its knot eyes but had no neck, so it could only circle around.

questions.q: What happened to Jack when the Saw-horse was spinning around?
options: Jack ran away into the trees
The horse bumped him and he tumbled onto the moss
questions.why: The prancing horse bumped Jack, who fell onto the moss by the road.

questions.q: Why didn't the Saw-horse obey when Tip shouted "Whoa!"?
options: It was being stubborn on purpose
It had no ears, so it could not hear him
questions.why: Jack pointed out that the animal had no ears.

questions.q: What happened to Tip's foot?
options: He stubbed it on a rock
The Saw-horse stamped a wooden leg down on it
questions.why: The Saw-horse brought a leg down hard on Tip's foot.

questions.q: What happened when Tip tied the Saw-horse to a tree with a cord?
options: It stepped backward and snapped the string
questions.why: The Saw-horse easily broke the cord by backing up.

questions.q: From what did Tip make the Saw-horse's ears?
questions.why: Tip carved the ears from bark with his knife.

questions.q: Why did Tip say he mustn't make the ears too big?
options: The horse would hear too much
The horse would become a donkey
questions.why: Tip joked that big ears would turn their horse into a donkey.

questions.q: Why did the Saw-horse suddenly bolt after the ears were put on?
options: Tip hit it with a stick
Jack's words were the first sounds it had heard, and they startled it
questions.why: Jack's remark that the ears looked handsome frightened the horse, which ran off.

questions.q: What finally stopped the runaway Saw-horse?
options: It stepped into a gopher-hole and tumbled over
questions.why: Its leg went into a gopher-hole and it fell on its back.

questions.q: After learning that 'whoa' means stop, what did the Saw-horse ask?
options: Whether a hole in the ground means to stop, too
questions.why: The horse asked if a hole also means stop; Tip said yes, unless you step over it.

questions.q: What was wrong when the Saw-horse said something seemed wrong with it?
questions.why: Tip told it, 'You're upside down,' and rolled it over.

questions.q: According to Tip's instructions, what does "Trot!" mean?
options: To go as fast as you can
questions.why: Tip taught: Whoa means stop, Get-Up means walk forward, Trot means go as fast as you can.

questions.q: Why wouldn't the Saw-horse let Jack hold onto its ears?
options: It said then it couldn't hear
questions.why: The Saw-horse protested that holding its ears would stop it from hearing.

questions.q: What did Tip make for Jack to hold onto while riding?
options: A handle made from the pepper-box
A sharpened post, hammered into the horse's back behind its head
questions.why: Tip cut a short limb, sharpened it, and drove it in with a rock.

questions.q: How did the Saw-horse feel as Tip hammered in the post?
options: It was in terrible pain and ran away
It said it didn't exactly hurt, but being jarred made it nervous
questions.why: The horse said the jarring made it quite nervous rather than hurting.

questions.q: What did Tip say his whistling meant?
options: That he was pretty well satisfied
questions.why: Tip explained that whistling only meant he was pleased.

questions.q: Why did Jack say he could not whistle?
options: He could not push his lips together, since his mouth was carved
He had never heard a whistle
questions.why: Jack said he would whistle if he could push his lips together and felt lacking.

questions.q: What did the sign-post on the yellow brick road say?
options: Ninety miles to the Emerald City
Nine miles to the Emerald City
questions.why: The sign read 'NINE MILES TO THE EMERALD CITY.'

questions.q: Why did the travelers stop for the night?
questions.why: Darkness was coming, so Tip decided to camp by the road.

questions.q: How did the Saw-horse spend the night?
options: Standing guard, since it could not sleep, to watch that no one came near
questions.why: Tip told the horse it could stand and keep watch since it could not sleep.

chapters.title: 6. Jack Pumpkinhead's Ride to the Emerald City

questions.q: What did Tip do when he woke at daybreak?
options: Bathed in a brook and ate bread and cheese
Built a fire and cooked eggs
questions.why: Tip washed in a brook and breakfasted before they started.

questions.q: By what time did Tip hope to reach the Emerald City?
options: By noon, if no accidents happened
questions.why: Tip said nine miles was a distance but they should arrive by noon.

questions.q: How did the colors of the countryside change as they traveled?
options: They stayed purple the whole way
From purple to lavender to greenish tones
questions.why: Nearing the Emerald City, the purple faded to lavender and then greenish colors.

questions.q: What blocked their way after about two miles?
questions.why: They came to a wide, swift river across the road.

questions.q: Why wouldn't the ferryman row them across?
options: They had no money to pay him
He was afraid of the Saw-horse
questions.why: Tip had no money, so the ferryman refused.

questions.q: When the ferryman refused to help, Jack said, 'What a nice man!' What does this show?
options: Jack does not yet understand people well and misjudges them
Jack wanted to stay with the ferryman
questions.why: The ferryman was unhelpful, so Jack's praise shows his simple, mistaken view of the world.

questions.q: How did the travelers get across the river?
options: They waited for a bridge to be built
They walked along the river bottom
The wooden Saw-horse swam with Tip on its back and Jack holding its tail
questions.why: Tip rode the floating horse while Jack held on behind, and the horse paddled across.

questions.q: After the crossing, which part of Tip was wet?
questions.why: Tip was wet below but dry above, while Jack was dripping.

questions.q: Why did Tip suggest they go faster after the river?
options: The wind would help dry their clothes
questions.why: Tip said a faster ride would dry them out.

questions.q: How did Tip become separated from Jack and the Saw-horse?
options: The branch-tail he was holding snapped and he fell into the dust
He stopped to talk to the ferryman
He fell asleep by the road
questions.why: Tip was running holding the tail; it broke and the horse raced on.

questions.q: Why wasn't Tip too worried after being left behind?
options: He knew the horse would come back
He planned to go home instead
The road would end at the gates of the Emerald City, so he would catch up
questions.why: Tip reasoned he would overtake them since the road ends at the city gates.

questions.q: What made Jack shout 'Whoa!'?
options: He feared they would crash into the high green wall of the city
A soldier ordered him to stop
questions.why: Jack saw the green wall ahead and cried 'Whoa' to avoid a collision.

questions.q: How did the Guardian of the Gates look?
options: Tall and thin, dressed in purple
Short and round, dressed all in green with a peaked hat and spectacles
An old woman in a black cloak
questions.why: The Guardian was a little, round man dressed in green.

questions.q: When asked his business in the city, what did Jack answer?
options: He had no idea what it was, but his father knew
questions.why: Jack said he couldn't think of his errand, and his father knew about it but was not there.

questions.q: Why did the Guardian decide Jack was not dangerous?
options: Jack showed him a letter from Tip
Folks do not smile so delightfully when they mean mischief
questions.why: The Guardian said people who mean mischief don't smile so delightfully.

questions.q: How did Jack explain his constant smile?
options: He was always happy to meet new people
The Powder of Life made him smile
It was carved on his face with a jackknife
He was trying to fool the Guardian
questions.why: Jack said he couldn't help it, since his smile was carved.

questions.q: Who was called to decide what to do with Jack?
options: The Soldier with the Green Whiskers
questions.why: The Guardian rang for the tall soldier whose green whiskers reached his knees.

questions.q: Why did the soldier say everyone must wear spectacles in the city?
options: It was the fashion, and they kept people from being blinded by the glitter
They were a gift from the Scarecrow
questions.why: The soldier explained spectacles were the fashion and protected against the glare.

questions.q: Why did the Guardian have to tie Jack's spectacles on?
options: The Saw-horse kept knocking them off
Jack's head was so big and his eyes so large that no pair fit properly
questions.why: The Guardian said he had no pair to cover Jack's eyes and his head was too big.

questions.q: Why was the Scarecrow willing to see Jack right away?
options: Tip had sent a message ahead
He was bored and had nothing else to do at the time
questions.why: The Scarecrow was at leisure and bored, so he had Jack brought to the throne room at once.

questions.q: What is the Scarecrow's head made of?
options: A small sack stuffed with straw
questions.why: The text describes his head as a small sack stuffed with straw, with a face painted on it.

questions.q: Why does the Scarecrow's painted face look wrinkled and thoughtful?
options: He is worried about the rebel army
His heavy jeweled crown presses down and wrinkles his brow
He had just been soaked in water
questions.why: The heavy golden crown makes his brow sag into wrinkles, giving him a thoughtful look.

questions.q: At first, why does the Scarecrow feel like resenting Jack Pumpkinhead?
options: He thinks Jack is laughing at him
questions.why: Jack's carved grin makes the Scarecrow think Jack is laughing at him.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow discover when he looks closely at Jack's smile?
options: It fades when Jack is sad
It is part of a mask Jack can take off
It is carved into the pumpkin, so Jack can't look serious even if he wants to
questions.why: Jack's features are carved into a permanent grin, so he can never look serious.

questions.q: Why does Jack believe he and the Scarecrow won't be able to understand each other?
options: He thinks people from different countries must speak different languages
The Scarecrow speaks only in signs
questions.why: Jack admits he thought they must speak different languages because they came from different countries.

questions.q: As the Scarecrow uses the word, what is an 'interpreter'?
options: A person who knows both languages and explains what each speaker means
questions.why: The Scarecrow explains that an interpreter understands both languages and tells each speaker what the other means.

questions.q: What 'sign' does the Scarecrow use to invite Jack to sit down?
options: He rolls an armchair behind Jack and pushes him into it
questions.why: The Scarecrow rolls an armchair behind Jack and pushes him so that he sprawls onto the cushions.

questions.q: The Scarecrow says, "I will bend, but not break, you will break, but not bend." What difference is he pointing out?
options: Jack is braver than he is
His straw body is floppy, while Jack's wooden body is stiff
questions.why: After Jack folds up awkwardly in the chair, the Scarecrow contrasts his own soft straw body with Jack's stiff wooden one.

questions.q: Who is brought in to be the interpreter?
questions.why: The soldier comes back with a girl the Scarecrow knows as "little Jellia Jamb."

questions.q: Why does Jellia say she understands the Gillikin language?
options: She was born in the North Country
questions.why: Jellia says she knows it because she was born in the North Country, the Gillikin land.

questions.q: What decorates Jellia Jamb's green satin slippers?
questions.why: Her green satin slippers have bunches of lettuce instead of bows or buckles.

questions.q: Instead of asking why Jack came to the city, what does Jellia first ask him?
questions.why: Jellia calls Jack a wonderful creature and asks, "Who made you?"

questions.q: Jack says a boy named Tip made him. What does Jellia tell the Scarecrow Jack said?
options: That the Scarecrow's brains seem to have come loose
That Jack wants to be king
That Jack comes from the Munchkin Country
questions.why: Jellia mischievously claims Jack said the King's brains seem to have come loose.

questions.q: How does the Scarecrow react to that false translation?
options: He moves uneasily and feels his head with his left hand
questions.why: The Scarecrow moves uneasily and feels his head with his left hand.

questions.q: Jack says he can't eat. What does Jellia pretend Jack said?
options: That he wants to go home
That one of the Scarecrow's eyes is painted larger than the other
That he is afraid of the soldier
questions.why: Jellia claims Jack asked whether the King knew one of his eyes was painted larger than the other.

questions.q: Which word best describes how Jellia acts as the interpreter?
questions.why: She makes up teasing "translations" that the speakers never said.

questions.q: What makes the Scarecrow suspect an interpreter isn't needed?
options: He realizes he understands Jack without her help
He reads a book about languages
questions.why: The Scarecrow asks Jellia how it is that he seems to understand Jack himself.

questions.q: What fact about Oz does Jellia reveal, laughing?
options: Each country of Oz has its own language
Only one language is spoken in all the land of Oz
Only the Wizard speaks every language
questions.why: Jellia says the languages are "one and the same" and that only one language is spoken in all of Oz.

questions.q: Why does the Scarecrow warn Jack "never to think"?
options: Unless you can think wisely, it is better to remain a dummy
Only kings are allowed to think
questions.why: He says that unless one can think wisely, it is better to remain a dummy, since Jack's poor thinking caused the mix-up.

questions.q: Why does the Scarecrow suggest that he and Jack become friends?
options: They both come from the Gillikin Country
They both love the game of quoits
They are both different from all ordinary people
questions.why: The Scarecrow says, "as we differ from all ordinary people, let us become friends."

questions.q: What problem does Tip have when this chapter begins?
options: He has eaten all his crackers and cheese and is very hungry
questions.why: About halfway to the Emerald City, Tip is very hungry because he has eaten all his crackers and cheese.

questions.q: How many colors are in General Jinjur's skirt?
questions.why: Her skirt is blue in front, yellow on the left, red in back, and purple on the right.

questions.q: What color is the waist (top) of Jinjur's dress?
questions.why: Her silk waist is emerald green.

questions.q: What does the girl by the roadside tell Tip to do?
options: Carry her lunch basket and eat from it if he is hungry
questions.why: She tells him to carry her basket and help himself to its contents if he is hungry.

questions.q: Why does Tip suspect the girl must be an important person?
options: She walks with quick steps and acts very decided and important
Soldiers salute her as she passes
questions.why: The way she moves, with quick steps and an air of decision and importance, makes Tip think she is a great personage.

questions.q: What does General Jinjur command?
questions.why: She tells Tip, "I command the Army of Revolt in this war."

questions.q: Where has Jinjur's army gathered?
options: On the banks of a river
In a forest clearing about a mile away
questions.why: They reach a large clearing in a forest where the army is waiting, about a mile away.

questions.q: Which is one reason Jinjur gives for conquering the Scarecrow?
options: He has been cruel to the people
The Emerald City has been ruled by men long enough
questions.why: Jinjur says the city "has been ruled by men long enough."

questions.q: What does Jinjur want to do with the city's gems and the royal treasury?
options: Use the gems as jewelry and buy new gowns for her army
Give them back to the Wizard
questions.why: She says the gems would be better used as jewelry and the money could buy every girl in her army new gowns.

questions.q: About how many girls are in the Army of Revolt?
questions.why: Four hundred young women have gathered in the clearing.

questions.q: How are the four companies of the army told apart?
options: By the colored strip on the front of their skirts, which shows their home country
questions.why: Each company wears the color of its home country on the front of the skirt: blue for Munchkin, red for Quadling, yellow for Winkie, purple for Gillikin.

questions.q: Why do all the girls in the army wear green waists?
options: It hides them in the forest
It stands for the Emerald City they plan to conquer
questions.why: The green waists represent the Emerald City they mean to conquer.

questions.q: What weapons does the army carry?
options: Two long knitting-needles stuck in their hair
questions.why: Each girl has two long, glittering knitting-needles stuck through the knot of her hair.

questions.q: What mistake does Tip make about the army at first?
options: He thinks they are Munchkin soldiers
He thinks they have no weapons
questions.why: Tip thinks the army is unarmed, but he is wrong, because they carry knitting-needles.

questions.q: While General Jinjur gives her speech from a tree stump, what are most of the girls doing?
options: Chattering too much to pay attention
questions.why: Tip sees that most of them are too busy chattering to listen to the General.

questions.q: What is Tip's job as the army marches?
options: He stays behind in the clearing
He carries baskets, wraps, and packages for the girls
questions.why: Tip follows, carrying baskets, wraps, and packages that girls in the army give him.

questions.q: How does the Guardian of the Gate first greet the army?
options: Pleasantly, not seeing any danger: "Good morning, my dears!"
By locking the gate at once
questions.why: With his hands in his pockets, he cheerfully asks, "Good morning, my dears! What can I do for you?"

questions.q: Jinjur says, "We are revolting!" and the Guardian answers, "You don't look it." What does his answer show?
options: He is scared of the girls
He does not take the girls seriously as a threat
He wants to join the army
He does not understand their language
questions.why: He looks at them admiringly and tells them to go home, which shows he doesn't see them as a danger.

questions.q: How does Jinjur get the keys to the city gate?
options: She bribes the Guardian with jewels
She tricks the Guardian into handing them over
The girls jab their knitting-needles near his face, and Jinjur takes the keys from his neck
She finds them lying on the ground
questions.why: While the girls threaten him with their needles, Jinjur snatches the keys from the chain around his neck.

questions.q: Why can't the Soldier with the Green Whiskers stop the army?
options: He has no key to the gate
His gun isn't loaded because he forgot where he hid the powder and shot
questions.why: He admits his gun isn't loaded because he has forgotten where he hid the powder and shot.

questions.q: What are the Scarecrow and Jack doing when Tip reaches the palace?
options: Playing a game of quoits in the courtyard
questions.why: Tip arrives while the Scarecrow and Jack are playing quoits in the courtyard.

questions.q: What news does the Soldier with the Green Whiskers bring?
questions.why: He cries out, "The City is conquered!"

questions.q: How does the Scarecrow react at first to the news?
options: He calmly says, "This is quite sudden," and asks the Soldier to bar the doors and windows
questions.why: He stays calm, orders the doors and windows barred, and keeps teaching Jack to throw a quoit.

questions.q: What does Jack call Tip when he sees him?
questions.why: Jack greets Tip as "noble parent," since Tip made him.

questions.q: The Soldier says, "Your Standing Army was running." What makes this line funny?
options: The army that is supposed to be 'standing' was really running away
The army was running a race
questions.why: It plays on the words: the 'Standing Army' was actually running from the girls.

questions.q: Why doesn't the Scarecrow mind much about losing his throne?
options: Ruling is a tiresome job, and the crown makes his head ache
He wants to go back to his cornfield
He is sure the Wizard will return
questions.why: He says ruling the Emerald City is tiresome and the crown makes his head ache.

questions.q: What news from Tip makes the Scarecrow decide he is really in danger?
options: The girls plan to lock him in a tower
The girls plan to send him to Mombi
The rebels plan to make a rag carpet of his outside and stuff sofa-cushions with his inside
The rebels plan to burn the palace
questions.why: After Tip tells him about the rag-carpet and sofa-cushion plan, the Scarecrow says, "Then I am really in danger."

questions.q: Where does the Scarecrow plan to escape to?
options: His friend the Tin Woodman, Emperor of the Winkies
questions.why: He wants to go to his friend the Tin Woodman, who rules the Winkies.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow do when Tip says the palace is surrounded?
options: He pauses to reflect, standing in a corner facing the wall for about five minutes
questions.why: He says it is good to pause and reflect in an emergency, then stands in a corner for about five minutes.

questions.q: Why is Jack worried about being a prisoner?
options: He is afraid of the dark
If the girls know how to cook, or if he is kept too long and spoils, he is done for
He will miss the game of quoits
questions.why: Jack fears the girls might cook him and worries that he could spoil if he is held prisoner for long.

questions.q: Where had the Soldier locked up the Saw-Horse?
questions.why: The Soldier had shut the Saw-Horse in the royal treasury.

questions.q: According to the Soldier, what did he feed the Saw-Horse?
questions.why: The Soldier says he gave it a heaping peck of sawdust, which is a joke, since the Saw-Horse is made of wood.

questions.q: Why does the Scarecrow leave the Soldier with the Green Whiskers behind?
options: The horse can't carry four, and he has little faith in a soldier who was conquered so easily
The Soldier wants to join Jinjur
The Soldier is too old to ride
questions.why: Tip points out that the horse can't carry four, and the Scarecrow says the easy conquest gives him little confidence in the Soldier.

questions.q: How does the Soldier plan to disguise himself?
options: By cutting off his green whiskers
questions.why: He says he will cut off his lovely green whiskers to disguise himself.

questions.q: Why are the three riders tied together and to the horse with a clothesline?
options: So the Saw-Horse can't throw them off
So they look like one creature
So they stay together, since if one falls off, all of them will
questions.why: The Scarecrow reasons, "Then if one falls off we will all fall off."

questions.q: What does Tip tell the Saw-Horse to do?
options: Find the Tin Woodman on his own
Run as fast as he can for the city gate and let nothing stop him
questions.why: Tip says, "Run as fast as you can for the gate of the City, and don't let anything stop you."

questions.q: What happens to Tip during the dash through the rebels?
options: He gets a small prick in his left arm that hurts for an hour
questions.why: One girl's needle gives Tip a small prick in his left arm, and it smarts for an hour.

questions.q: Why do the knitting-needles do no harm to the Scarecrow and Jack?
options: Their bodies are straw and wood, not flesh, so the needles can't hurt them
questions.why: The needles have no effect on the Scarecrow and Jack because of what they are made of.

questions.q: Who is the new Guardian of the Gate that the Saw-Horse knocks over?
options: The Soldier with the Green Whiskers
A fussy little woman appointed by Jinjur
questions.why: The Saw-Horse bowls over the new Guardian, a fussy little woman whom General Jinjur appointed.

questions.q: How does the wild ride end?
options: They reach the Tin Woodman's palace
The Saw-Horse leaps into a wide river
questions.why: At the bank of a wide river, the Saw-Horse jumps, and they all land in the water.

chapters.title: 10. The Journey to the Tin Woodman

questions.q: After Tip shouts, "Keep still, you fool!" what does the Saw-Horse do?
options: Stops struggling and floats calmly, like a raft
questions.why: The horse stops struggling, and its wooden body floats easily.

questions.q: Tip explains that "fool" is "a term of reproach." What does "reproach" mean?
questions.why: Tip says people use the word when they are angry, so a reproach is an expression of blame.

questions.q: How do the travelers get out of the river?
options: They swing to shore on a vine
The Saw-Horse paddles to a low place on the bank and climbs out
Glinda lifts them out with magic
questions.why: Tip tells the horse to paddle to shore, and it climbs out where the bank is low.

questions.q: What has happened to the Scarecrow's straw after the wild ride?
options: It has shaken down into his lower body, so his top half looks like an empty sack
questions.why: The straw has packed down into his legs and lower body, leaving his top half limp.

questions.q: With his face crushed into wrinkles under his crown, what does the Scarecrow look like?
questions.why: The narrator says his wrinkled face makes him look like a Japanese pug dog.

questions.q: What happened to Jack Pumpkinhead in the river?
options: His pumpkin head came off and floated away
questions.why: Jack's head came off, and Tip sees the pumpkin bobbing far out on the water.

questions.q: How does Tip get Jack's head back?
options: He waits for it to float closer and pulls it in with a long pole
A fish pushes it to shore
questions.why: Tip waits with a long pole until the pumpkin drifts close enough to reach.

questions.q: Once his head is back on, what is Jack's first worry?
questions.why: Jack asks, "I wonder if water is liable to spoil pumpkins?"

questions.q: According to Tip, when would water spoil a pumpkin?
questions.why: Tip says water won't spoil pumpkins unless it is boiling.

questions.q: How does Tip repair the Scarecrow?
options: He sews on a new head
He dries the straw in the sun and restuffs him evenly
He takes him to a tailor
questions.why: Tip spreads the straw in the sun to dry, then stuffs the Scarecrow evenly and smooths his face.

questions.q: What advantage of being a Scarecrow does the Scarecrow mention?
options: If friends are nearby to repair him, nothing very serious can happen to him
questions.why: He says that with friends nearby to make repairs, nothing very serious can happen to him.

questions.q: Tip says, "Care once killed a cat." What does Jack's reply show about him?
options: He is making a clever joke
He takes the saying literally and is glad he isn't a cat
questions.why: Jack answers that he is glad he isn't a cat, which shows he took the saying literally.

questions.q: Jack asks the Saw-Horse, "Aren't you a little hoarse?" Why does this cause trouble?
options: "Hoarse" (rough-voiced) sounds like "horse," and the Saw-Horse takes it as an insult
questions.why: The Saw-Horse takes Jack's remark about his gruff voice as an insult and asks Tip to protect him.

questions.q: The Saw-Horse says Jack "loses his head too easily." Why is this funny?
options: Jack's head really did come off, and the phrase also means getting upset too easily
questions.why: The phrase usually means panicking, but Jack's head had actually just come off in the river.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow say he once did on a grassy knoll along the way?
options: He saved Dorothy from the Wicked Witch's Stinging Bees
questions.why: He recalls saving Dorothy from the Stinging Bees of the Wicked Witch of the West.

questions.q: Who is Nick Chopper?
options: The Soldier with the Green Whiskers
questions.why: When Tip asks, the Scarecrow explains that Nick Chopper is the Tin Woodman.

questions.q: What did Nick Chopper destroy in this area, according to the Scarecrow?
questions.why: The Scarecrow points out where Nick Chopper destroyed the Wicked Witch's Grey Wolves.

questions.q: Why does the Scarecrow say Jack needn't worry much about the Winged Monkeys?
options: They are now slaves of Glinda the Good, who owns the Golden Cap
They live far away in the south
questions.why: He explains that Glinda owns the Golden Cap that commands the monkeys.

questions.q: What trait does Jack show again and again in this chapter?
options: Worry about anything that might harm a pumpkin
questions.why: Jack keeps asking whether water, bees, or monkeys harm pumpkins.

questions.q: How does the chapter end?
options: They reach the Tin Woodman's palace
Tip falls asleep on the grass, using the Scarecrow as a pillow
questions.why: When night falls, Tip lies down and sleeps with the Scarecrow as his pillow, since the others don't need sleep.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow gather for Tip's breakfast?
options: A double handful of ripe berries
questions.why: The Scarecrow picks a double handful of ripe berries with his clumsy fingers.

questions.q: How long do the travelers ride before they reach a hilltop and see their destination?
questions.why: After traveling for an hour, they reach a hilltop.

questions.q: What do they see from the hilltop?
options: The City of the Winkies and the tall domes of the Emperor's palace
questions.why: They see the City of the Winkies, with the tall domes of the Emperor's palace rising above the houses.

questions.q: What point does Tip make about the Tin Woodman's title of "Emperor"?
options: The title belongs to the Scarecrow
An emperor rules an empire, but the Winkie Country is only a kingdom
questions.why: Tip says an emperor should rule an empire, while the Winkie Country is only a kingdom.

questions.q: Why does the Scarecrow tell Tip not to mention this to the Tin Woodman?
options: It would hurt the proud Tin Woodman's feelings, since he likes being called Emperor
The Tin Woodman would get angry and use his axe
questions.why: He says the Tin Woodman is proud, likes being called Emperor, and would have his feelings badly hurt.

questions.q: What is the old Winkie servant wearing?
questions.why: The elderly Winkie wears a uniform of silver cloth.

questions.q: Why can't the Emperor see visitors that morning, at first?
options: It is his day for being polished, and he is smeared with putz-pomade
questions.why: The servant explains that it is his polishing day and he is thickly smeared with putz-pomade.

questions.q: What has the Tin Woodman recently had done to himself?
questions.why: The servant says the Emperor has had himself nickel-plated.

questions.q: The Scarecrow says, "If his wit bears the same polish, how sparkling it must be!" What does he mean?
options: He hopes his friend's mind is as bright and clever as his shiny new body
He thinks the polish will ruin his friend's mind
He wants to be polished too
He thinks the Tin Woodman is dull
questions.why: He is joking that a shiny body might come with a brilliant, 'sparkling' wit.

questions.q: What stands on the center table in the ante-room?
options: A large silver oil-can engraved with scenes from past adventures
questions.why: The table holds a large silver oil-can engraved with the adventures of the Tin Woodman, Dorothy, the Lion, and the Scarecrow.

questions.q: What does the large painting on the wall show?
options: The Wizard of Oz giving the Tin Woodman a heart
questions.why: A large painting shows the Wizard presenting the Tin Woodman with a heart.

questions.q: What problem does the Tin Woodman's loving hug cause?
options: It smears putz-pomade all over the Scarecrow
questions.why: Still covered in polish, the Tin Woodman leaves blotches of putz-pomade on the Scarecrow.

questions.q: How does the Tin Woodman offer to fix the mess?
options: By sending the Scarecrow to his Imperial Laundry
By giving the Scarecrow new clothes
questions.why: He says, "I'll send you to my Imperial Laundry, and you'll come out as good as new."

questions.q: Why does the Tin Woodman say Jack is worthy to join their "select society"?
questions.why: He says Jack is not very substantial but certainly unusual, and therefore worthy.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman suggest Jack could do to keep his head from spoiling?
options: Have it canned so it will keep
Trade it for a tin head
questions.why: He says Jack could have his head canned before it spoils, so it would keep indefinitely.

questions.q: The Tin Woodman says, "Do not... dampen today's sun with the showers of tomorrow." What does this mean?
options: Don't let worries about the future spoil the present
questions.why: He is telling Jack not to let fear of spoiling someday ruin a happy day now.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the engraved star on the Tin Woodman's left breast?
options: It shows where his heart is and covers the patch the Wizard made
It is a medal for bravery
It covers a dent from a Grey Wolf
questions.why: He says the star shows where his heart lies and neatly covers the Wizard's patch.

questions.q: What news does Tip add about the rebels?
options: They have left the Emerald City
He heard some of them say they plan to march on the Tin Woodman's castle and city
They are sorry and want peace
questions.why: Tip says he heard some of the girls plan to march and capture the Tin Woodman's castle and city.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman decide to do?
options: Build a wall around his city
Go at once to retake the Emerald City, with no army but his friends and his axe
Hide the Scarecrow in his palace
questions.why: He says they need no army; the group and his gleaming axe are enough to frighten the rebels.

questions.q: When the Tin Woodman says "We four," why does Jack correct him to "We five"?
options: A Winkie servant will join them
The Saw-Horse is brave and fearless and should be counted
questions.why: Jack says, "We five. The Saw-Horse is brave and fearless."

chapters.title: 12. Mr. H. M. Woggle-Bug, T. E.

questions.q: Why is General Jinjur worried at the start of this chapter?
options: She fears the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman will join forces against her
Her army wants to go home
questions.why: She knows it would mean danger for her if the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman joined forces.

questions.q: Whom does Jinjur call on for help?
options: The Soldier with the Green Whiskers
questions.why: Jinjur sends for Mombi and promises her rewards.

questions.q: Why is Mombi eager to help Jinjur?
options: Mombi is furious that Tip tricked her, escaped, and stole the Powder of Life
questions.why: Mombi is angry with Tip for deceiving her, running away, and stealing the Powder of Life.

questions.q: Where does Mombi go to work her magic against the travelers?
options: A locked room high in a palace tower
questions.why: She shuts herself in a room high in a tower to practice her magic.

questions.q: What is the first sign that something strange is happening on the journey?
options: The Tin Woodman thinks they are lost, although he should know every step of the way
questions.why: The Tin Woodman says he should know the journey by heart but fears they have lost their way.

questions.q: What suddenly surrounds the travelers?
options: A field of tall sunflowers that whirl like windmills
questions.why: They are surrounded by tall stalks topped with giant sunflowers that spin like little windmills.

questions.q: Why can't the travelers tell which way to go in the sunflower field?
options: The dazzling colors and whirling flowers make them dizzy
The flowers are too thick to see through
questions.why: The flowers' spinning and blinding red and gold colors keep them from choosing a direction.

questions.q: What do the travelers see when the sunflowers stop spinning?
options: A girl's face with a mocking smile in each flower
questions.why: Each flower has a girl's face in the center, smiling mockingly and then laughing.

questions.q: Why won't the Tin Woodman chop down the sunflowers after all?
options: He thinks it would be heartless to chop down such pretty creatures
Tip orders him to stop and he always obeys
The flowers are too tough to cut
questions.why: He drops his axe and says it would be heartless to cut down the pretty creatures.

questions.q: What does Tip believe is going on?
options: The flowers are real girls who were turned into plants
Someone like Mombi is playing a magic trick, and the flowers might not be there at all
They have wandered into Glinda's garden
questions.why: Tip says it is magic, like tricks old Mombi has played, and probably only an illusion.

questions.q: Why can't the Scarecrow just shut his eyes and walk through?
options: He is afraid of the dark
He needs to guide the others
His eyes are painted on and have no lids
questions.why: The Scarecrow points out that his painted eyes have no lids to close.

questions.q: How do the travelers finally get past the sunflowers?
options: The Tin Woodman chops a path
They wait until the flowers fall asleep
They go back the way they came
Jack rides the Saw-Horse boldly forward, and Tip holds its stubby tail and follows with his eyes closed
questions.why: Jack rides boldly forward on the Saw-Horse while Tip grasps its stub tail and follows with closed eyes, and the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman come last.

questions.q: What do the travelers find when they look back?
options: Not a trace of the sunflower field is left
questions.why: When they look back, not a trace of the sunflower field remains.

questions.q: Tip thinks the sunflowers might be "an illusion." What is an illusion?
options: Something that seems real but isn't
questions.why: The sunflowers vanish once the travelers pass, so they only seemed to be real.

questions.q: Why does the Scarecrow decide to steer by the sun?
options: The Tin Woodman told him to
Witchcraft can't change the sun's course, so it is a reliable guide
questions.why: Since the landscape looked changed, he reasons that witchcraft cannot alter the sun's course.

questions.q: What causes the next accident?
options: The Saw-Horse steps into a rabbit hole and falls
questions.why: The Saw-Horse steps into a rabbit hole, tumbles, and throws Jack high into the air.

questions.q: Why can't the Tin Woodman make the Saw-Horse a new leg right away?
options: There are no trees, or even shrubs, for miles around
questions.why: He says he could make a new leg if there were trees nearby, but there isn't even a shrub for miles.

questions.q: When the Tin Woodman asks if his broken leg hurts, what does the Saw-Horse say?
options: Not at all, but his pride is hurt that his body is so brittle
He can't feel anything and doesn't care
questions.why: The Saw-Horse says it doesn't hurt, but his pride is injured to find his body so brittle.

questions.q: What do the letters "H. M." and "T. E." on the Woggle-Bug's card stand for?
questions.why: The Woggle-Bug explains that H. M. means Highly Magnified and T. E. means Thoroughly Educated.

questions.q: What does the Woggle-Bug say about surprising people?
options: He is sorry he frightened them
He hates to be stared at
He wants to hide from humans
He enjoys it and feels he deserves curiosity and admiration
questions.why: He says it pleases him to surprise people and that he deserves both curiosity and admiration.

questions.q: How does the Woggle-Bug say he began his life?
options: As a prince under a spell
As a giant insect from a far country
As a toy brought to life by magic powder
questions.why: He admits he 'was born an ordinary Woggle-Bug' who crawled among the grass.

questions.q: What did the Woggle-Bug do for food before his education?
options: Ate crumbs from the schoolchildren's lunches
questions.why: He describes hunting smaller insects for food in his former life.

questions.q: What drew the Woggle-Bug to the country schoolhouse?
options: He was looking for a warm place to escape a storm
A child carried him inside in a jar
He wanted to eat the flies near the windows
His curiosity about the humming sound of pupils saying their lessons
questions.why: Curiosity led him to the schoolhouse where he heard students humming their lessons.

questions.q: Where did the Woggle-Bug hide in the schoolhouse?
options: In a nest between two bricks near the hearth
Behind a map on the wall
questions.why: He found 'a charming nest between two bricks' by the hearth.

questions.q: What was the name of the schoolmaster?
questions.why: The text names the schoolmaster Professor Nowitall.

questions.q: How did the Woggle-Bug become educated?
options: By reading books in the school library at night
By eating the pages of a dictionary
By listening to the Professor's lectures to his pupils for many months
questions.why: Hidden by the hearth, he listened to the lectures and absorbed their knowledge.

questions.q: The Woggle-Bug puts 'T.E.' on his cards. What do the letters stand for?
questions.why: He explains 'T.E.' means 'Thoroughly Educated.'

questions.q: How did the Woggle-Bug become so large?
options: He ate a growing potion from the Professor's desk
Mombi cast a spell on him
He grew slowly over three years of eating well
The Professor used a magnifying-glass to throw his image on a screen in a highly-magnified condition
questions.why: The Professor said he would 'throw the insect upon a screen in a highly-magnified condition.'

questions.q: Why did the Professor call the Woggle-Bug a special find?
options: He said it was dangerous and must be destroyed
He said it was the school's lost pet
He said it was a very rare and interesting specimen
He said it could speak every language
questions.why: The Professor announced he had captured 'a very rare and interesting specimen.'

questions.q: What did the magnified Woggle-Bug do that caused the girls to fall out of the window?
options: He stood upright and politely bowed
He began to recite a lecture
questions.why: His polite bow startled a girl on the windowsill, who fell backward and pulled her companion with her.

questions.q: What happened right after the girls fell out of the window?
options: The Professor locked the Woggle-Bug in a box
The Professor and the pupils rushed outside to see if the girls were hurt
The girls climbed back in laughing
The Woggle-Bug shrank back to normal size
questions.why: The Professor ran out to check on the children and the students followed, leaving the Bug alone.

questions.q: Why was the Woggle-Bug able to escape from the schoolhouse?
options: The Professor let him go as a reward
Everyone had rushed outside, leaving him alone in the magnified state
He dug a tunnel under the hearth
He was carried out by the two girls
questions.why: Left alone in the schoolroom, he realized he could simply walk out while magnified.

questions.q: How did the Woggle-Bug get his stylish clothes?
options: A grateful tailor gave them to him after he saved the tailor's ninth life
He stole them from a clothesline
The Professor dressed him for display
He sewed them himself from school curtains
questions.why: He says he saved 'the ninth life of a tailor,' who furnished his costume in thanks.

questions.q: According to the Woggle-Bug, tailors are like cats because they
questions.why: He says tailors have, 'like cats, nine lives.'

questions.q: What does the Woggle-Bug plan to do in the Emerald City?
options: Give a course of lectures on the 'Advantages of Magnification'
questions.why: He intends to lecture to select audiences on the 'Advantages of Magnification.'

questions.q: What travel problem did the group need to solve in this chapter?
options: The Tin Woodman had rusted in the rain
The Scarecrow had lost his straw
The Sawhorse had a broken leg, and stiff-jointed Jack needed to ride
They were lost in a forest
questions.why: The Sawhorse could not travel on a broken leg, and the stiff-jointed Pumpkinhead needed a ride.

questions.q: What clever solution did the Woggle-Bug propose?
options: Carry the Sawhorse on their backs
Use one of Jack's legs to make a new leg for the Sawhorse that would carry him
Use Tip's powder to grow a new leg
questions.why: He reasoned that if Jack rides, he doesn't need his leg, so it can become the horse's leg.

questions.q: Which of Jack's legs was cut off, and who did it?
options: His left leg, by the Tin Woodman
His right leg, by the Tin Woodman
His right leg, by the Scarecrow
questions.why: Jack's 'left leg' was 'amputated by the Tin Woodman and whittled down.'

questions.q: When the Sawhorse calls Jack 'flimsy' and compares him to a jumping-jack, what does this show about the Sawhorse?
options: He is proud and grumpy about being mended with a leg he thinks is inferior
He is grateful and wants to thank Jack
He is afraid Jack will fall off
He is joking to cheer everyone up
questions.why: The Sawhorse complains the new leg is a disgrace and insults Jack's build, showing wounded pride.

questions.q: How was one-legged Jack kept safe on the Sawhorse for the journey?
options: The Tin Woodman held him in place
He was tied to his seat with cords
He was glued with pumpkin sap
questions.why: They 'tied him to his seat with cords, so that he could not possibly fall off.'

questions.q: Why did the Sawhorse limp at the start of the chapter?
options: His new leg was too short
His new leg was a little too long
A stone was stuck in his hoof
Jack was too heavy for him
questions.why: The text says 'his new leg was a trifle too long.'

questions.q: How did the group fix the Sawhorse's limp?
options: The Scarecrow stuffed straw under the other legs
They swapped the leg for a branch
The Tin Woodman chopped the leg shorter with his axe
questions.why: They halted 'while the Tin Woodman chopped it down with his axe.'

questions.q: The Woggle-Bug jokes that if he rode the Sawhorse, it would become a 'horse-and-buggy.' What kind of joke is this?
questions.why: The joke plays on his name, Woggle-Bug, and the word 'buggy'; he himself calls such jokes puns.

questions.q: How did Tip react to the Woggle-Bug's joke?
options: He said the joke was poor and as old as it was poor
He wrote it down to remember
questions.why: Tip says 'your joke is a poor one, and as old as it is poor.'

questions.q: What did the Scarecrow suggest was wrong with the Woggle-Bug's brains?
options: That he was over-educated and his brains were slightly tangled
That he had no brains at all
That his brains were made of sawdust
That he had borrowed his brains from the Wizard
questions.why: The Scarecrow suggests he is 'over-educated' with 'slightly tangled' brains.

questions.q: Why did the Woggle-Bug promise to 'restrain' himself?
options: The Sawhorse refused to carry him
The Tin Woodman threatened him with his axe if he kept making such jokes
questions.why: After the Tin Woodman's warning about his culture getting 'leaky,' the frightened Woggle-Bug promised to restrain himself.

questions.q: In context, 'I will endeavor to restrain myself' most nearly means
options: I will try to hold myself back
I will try to speak louder
questions.why: 'Endeavor' means try and 'restrain' means hold back, from the Woggle-Bug's promise to stop joking.

questions.q: How did the Tin Woodman know they had come to a Field Mouse village?
options: He noticed many small round holes in the grassy meadow
He saw a sign on a post
questions.why: He noticed small round holes in the meadow and identified the village.

questions.q: How did the Tin Woodman call the Queen of the Field Mice?
options: He knocked on her door with his axe
He shouted her name three times
He blew a shrill note on a silver whistle
He left a note by her hole
questions.why: 'The Tin Woodman blew a shrill note upon a silver whistle.'

questions.q: Why was the Queen of the Field Mice willing to help the travelers?
options: The Scarecrow promised her a palace
Mombi had ordered her to help
She wanted to see the Emerald City
The Tin Woodman had once saved her life
questions.why: The text notes she came because 'the Tin Woodman had once saved her life.'

questions.q: What did the Queen of the Field Mice wear?
questions.why: The Queen emerged wearing a tiny golden crown.

questions.q: How many field mice did the Scarecrow ask to take along?
questions.why: He asked to take 'a dozen' of her subjects, and she called twelve mice.

questions.q: Where were the mice to hide during the trip?
options: In the Tin Woodman's funnel hat
Inside the straw that stuffed the Scarecrow's body
questions.why: They were to hide 'in the straw which stuffs my body.'

questions.q: What were the mice supposed to do when the Scarecrow unbuttoned his jacket?
options: Rush out and scamper home, helping him regain his throne
questions.why: He said they would 'rush out and scamper home again,' helping him regain his throne.

questions.q: Who created the obstacles the travelers faced on the way?
questions.why: The obstacles were 'thrown in their way by the arts of old Mombi.'

questions.q: Which obstacle did the travelers meet FIRST?
questions.why: The order was river, granite wall, forty whirling roads, then fire.

questions.q: How did the travelers get past Mombi's obstacles?
options: The Tin Woodman chopped through them
They followed the Queen, who walked straight through them because they were not real
They waited until the obstacles disappeared overnight
questions.why: The obstacles were 'cleverly contrived deceptions,' and the Queen led them straight through.

questions.q: Why was the Scarecrow especially frightened by the sheet of flame?
options: He had never seen fire before
He is made of straw and would burn quickly
It was blocking the only road home
The mice in his straw were afraid of light
questions.why: He cried that if the fire reached him he would 'be gone in no time.'

questions.q: Which character stayed calm when the fire appeared?
questions.why: Only the Tin Woodman kept calm and told the others to watch the Queen walk through unharmed.

questions.q: What lesson does the Scarecrow state after they pass through the fire?
options: Magic is the best way to solve problems
Fire can never hurt a brave person
All magic is unnatural and should be feared and avoided
Education is more powerful than magic
questions.why: He says 'All magic is unnatural, and for that reason is to be feared and avoided.'

questions.q: Who guarded the gateway of the Emerald City when the travelers arrived?
options: Two girls of the Army of Revolt
The Soldier with the Green Whiskers
questions.why: The text describes 'two girls of the Army of Revolt' at the gate.

questions.q: What weapons did the Army of Revolt girls use?
questions.why: They opposed the travelers 'by drawing the knitting-needles from their hair.'

questions.q: Why was the Tin Woodman not afraid of the girl guards?
options: He knew they were his friends
He was hiding behind the Sawhorse
At worst they could only scratch his nickel-plate
questions.why: He says 'At the worst they can but scratch my beautiful nickel-plate.'

questions.q: What made the guards run away screaming?
options: The Tin Woodman swinging his axe in wide circles as he advanced
questions.why: He swung his axe in circles and advanced, and the girls fled.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow praise about his friend 'Nick' (the Tin Woodman)?
options: His kind heart and his sharp axe
questions.why: The Scarecrow says 'Nothing can resist your kind heart and your sharp axe.'

questions.q: What unusual sight did the travelers see in the city streets?
options: Men doing housework while women sat talking and laughing
questions.why: Men swept, dusted, and washed dishes while women sat gossiping.

questions.q: What did the tired man pushing a baby-carriage explain?
options: The city was preparing for a festival
There had been a revolution, and the women were running things
questions.why: He said they had 'had a revolution' and the women were running things to suit themselves.

questions.q: When the man says, 'Perhaps the women are made of cast-iron,' what does he mean?
options: Housework is so tiring that the women must have been extra tough to do it
The women had turned into statues
questions.why: He says housework is wearing out every man, so he jokes the women must have been made of tough iron.

questions.q: Why did the Scarecrow and Tip feel uneasy as they walked toward the palace?
options: They were lost in the streets
The soldiers stepped aside too easily, so it seemed like a trap
questions.why: Tip warns 'It's too easy, altogether,' and the Scarecrow fears a trap.

questions.q: What had happened to the marble steps of the palace?
options: They had been smashed into pieces
They had been covered in flowers
The rebels had pried out the emeralds, leaving tiny holes
questions.why: The steps showed tiny holes where emeralds had been removed by the rebels.

questions.q: What was Jinjur doing when the travelers entered the throne room?
options: Knitting a scarf by the window
Marching her soldiers in the courtyard
Sitting on the throne eating caramels, wearing the Scarecrow's second-best crown
questions.why: She had 'the Scarecrow's second-best crown upon her head' and a box of caramels in her lap.

questions.q: What is Jinjur's argument for why she is Queen?
options: The Wizard chose her before he left
The throne belongs to whoever is able to take it
questions.why: She says 'The throne belongs to whoever is able to take it.'

questions.q: The Scarecrow accuses Jinjur of 'treason.' In context, treason means
options: a crime of betraying or overthrowing one's ruler
questions.why: He charges her with treason for sitting on his throne, and she turns the charge back on anyone who opposes her.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman suggest doing about Jinjur?
options: Giving her jewels and sending her away happy
questions.why: His kind suggestion is to give her jewels and let her go happily; Tip suggested the closet and the Sawhorse the shaking.

questions.q: What signal did Jinjur give to spring her trap?
options: She clapped her hands three times
questions.why: She 'clapped her pretty hands together thrice, as if for a signal.'

questions.q: Why was the loss of the Tin Woodman's axe so important?
options: It was a gift from Glinda
It was the group's main means of defending themselves
It held the Powder of Life
questions.why: The axe had driven off the guards; once it was snatched, the group was surrounded and helpless.

questions.q: What did Jinjur plan to do with Tip?
options: Return him to old Mombi, who she said he belonged to
questions.why: She said the boy 'belongs to old Mombi and must be restored to her keeping.'

questions.q: What did Jinjur plan for the Scarecrow?
questions.why: Her orders included burning the Scarecrow; the pumpkin was for tarts and the Tin Woodman for goats.

questions.q: Why did the Army of Revolt suddenly flee from the throne room?
options: The Tin Woodman got his axe back
Grey mice leaped out of the Scarecrow's jacket and frightened them
questions.why: When the Scarecrow unbuttoned his jacket, mice scampered out and the girls fled screaming.

questions.q: After the soldiers fled, what did the Scarecrow order the group to do, and why?
options: Bar all the palace entrances so they would have time to think
Chase Jinjur out of the city
questions.why: He said 'Let us bar all the entrances to the palace! Then we shall have time to think.'

chapters.title: 16. The Scarecrow Takes Time to Think

questions.q: Where do the companions gather at the start of this chapter?
options: In the throne room of the palace
questions.why: They reassemble in the throne room for their council.

questions.q: What surprising admission does the Scarecrow make at the start?
options: That Jinjur is right in claiming to be Queen, so he must be wrong
That he never wanted to be King
That he is afraid of mice
That he has lost his brains
questions.why: He says 'the girl Jinjur is quite right in claiming to be Queen. And if she is right, then I am wrong.'

questions.q: What argument does the Woggle-Bug make against Jinjur?
options: The Scarecrow was King first, so Jinjur is the interloper
Jinjur is too young to rule
Jinjur stole the Powder of Life
questions.why: The Woggle-Bug points out the Scarecrow was King first.

questions.q: In context, an 'interloper' is someone who
options: pushes in where they have no right to be
questions.why: The Woggle-Bug uses the word for Jinjur, who took a throne that was not hers.

questions.q: What did Tip see when he looked out of the window?
options: The Emerald City empty and quiet
A double row of girl soldiers surrounding the palace
questions.why: Tip reports 'The palace is surrounded by a double row of girl soldiers.'

questions.q: What did Tip's view out the window prove?
options: That they had not really won and were still prisoners
That they could easily walk out
questions.why: Nick Chopper agrees 'Jinjur is still the Queen, and we are her prisoners.'

questions.q: Why is Jack Pumpkinhead worried?
options: He has lost his new leg
Jinjur threatened to make his pumpkin head into tarts
He is afraid of the Woggle-Bug's puns
questions.why: Jack recalls Jinjur's threat to turn him into tarts.

questions.q: How does the Woggle-Bug describe himself when upset about becoming goulash?
options: As the bravest insect in Oz
As the only Highly Magnified and Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug in the world
questions.why: He calls himself 'the only Highly Magnified and Thoroughly Educated Woggle-Bug in the wide, wide world!'

questions.q: What new danger does Tip point out?
options: They might starve while trapped in the palace
The river might flood the city
questions.why: Tip warns that they may starve.

questions.q: How does the Tin Woodman respond when the Woggle-Bug suggests eating Jack?
options: He agrees it is a clever idea
He asks, 'Are we cannibals? Or are we faithful friends?'
He offers to cook the pumpkin
questions.why: His protest shows his kind heart and loyalty to Jack.

questions.q: What fell out of Tip's pocket?
options: The pepper-box holding the Powder of Life
questions.why: A pepper-box fell out, and Tip explains it holds his Powder of Life.

questions.q: How much Powder of Life does Tip say is left?
questions.why: Tip says 'there's only about one dose left.'

questions.q: Which two characters had already been brought to life with the powder?
options: The Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman
questions.why: The powder had animated both Jack and the Sawhorse.
