questions.q: What did Tip do to help the Scarecrow think?
options: Cut the stitches holding the crown onto his head
questions.why: 'Tip soon cut the stitches that had fastened the crown to the Scarecrow's head.'

questions.q: According to the Scarecrow, who wore the crown before the Wizard?
questions.why: He says the former King 'named Pastoria, lost the crown to the Wonderful Wizard.'

questions.q: What does the history of the crown suggest about power in the Emerald City?
options: The same family has always ruled
Rulers have often lost the crown to someone else
The crown is cursed to fall apart
Only wizards may wear the crown
questions.why: The crown passed from Pastoria to the Wizard to the Scarecrow to Jinjur, showing how power keeps changing hands.

questions.q: How long did the Scarecrow take to think?
options: What seemed a very long time to his anxious friends
questions.why: The text says he sat up 'after what seemed a very long time indeed to the anxious watchers.'

questions.q: What escape plan did the Scarecrow finally announce?
options: Dig a tunnel under the city walls
Escape through the air in a winged machine brought to life with the powder
Wait for the army to leave
questions.why: He declares 'We must escape through the air!' with a winged machine that Tip will animate.

questions.q: Who was to build the flying machine?
questions.why: The Tin Woodman was to build a machine with 'good strong wings.'

questions.q: What did the Tin Woodman use to make Jack's new leg, and how did Jack feel about it?
options: A broom handle; Jack was embarrassed
A palm branch; Jack was worried
A carved leg from a mahogany center-table; Jack was very proud
A tin pipe; Jack was angry
questions.why: He fitted a beautifully carved mahogany table leg to Jack, who became very proud of it.

chapters.title: 17. The Astonishing Flight of the Gump

questions.q: Where do the adventurers gather to build their flying machine?
questions.why: They assemble on the palace roof with their materials.

questions.q: What did the Woggle-Bug bring, and where had it been?
options: A sofa from the throne room
A Gump's head that hung over the mantelpiece in the great hallway
questions.why: He took the Gump's head 'from its position over the mantelpiece in the great hallway.'

questions.q: How is the Gump's head described?
options: Like an elk's head with wide antlers, an upturned nose, and billy-goat whiskers
Like a lion's head with a golden mane
Like an eagle's head with a sharp beak
Like a horse's head with a long mane
questions.why: It had wide-spreading antlers, an upturned nose, and whiskers like a billy-goat's.

questions.q: What did Tip and the Sawhorse carry to the roof first?
questions.why: Tip and the Sawhorse struggled to bring up a sofa.

questions.q: What did Jack Pumpkinhead bring?
questions.why: The Pumpkinhead brought a broom.

questions.q: What happened to the Scarecrow as he carried the ropes and clotheslines?
options: He dropped them off the roof
He got tangled up in them
questions.why: The Scarecrow carried ropes and clotheslines and became tangled in them.

questions.q: Where did the Tin Woodman get the four large leaves?
options: From a huge palm-tree in the courtyard that was the pride of the city
From a tree in the forest
questions.why: He cut them 'from a huge palm-tree that was the pride of all the inhabitants of the Emerald City.'

questions.q: What penalty does the Scarecrow say goes with cutting leaves from the royal palm?
options: Paying a fine of one emerald
Being killed seven times and then imprisoned for life
questions.why: He says the penalty is 'to be killed seven times and afterward imprisoned for life.'

questions.q: What makes the Scarecrow's statement about the penalty humorous?
options: It is impossible for a person to be killed seven times and then imprisoned
The Tin Woodman is the King
questions.why: The absurd punishment of being killed seven times and then jailed shows Baum's playful humor.

questions.q: Why did Tip suggest getting a second sofa?
options: With just one sofa, the machine might tip sideways and riders could fall off
Jinjur's soldiers wanted the first sofa
The Gump's head was too heavy
questions.why: The Tin Woodman noted sideways tipping could cause falls, and Tip suggested the second sofa from downstairs.

questions.q: How were the two sofas joined?
options: They were tied with the Scarecrow's straw
They were bound together with ropes
questions.why: The two sofas were bound together with ropes to form the body.

questions.q: What part of the machine did the palm leaves become?
questions.why: The Tin Woodman fastened the palm leaves as wings, 'two on each side.'

questions.q: Why did Jack suggest adding the broom?
options: To be a tail for steering, like a bird's
questions.why: Jack proposed the broom as a tail, and the Scarecrow agreed birds use tails as a rudder.

questions.q: In context, a 'rudder' is
questions.why: The Scarecrow says birds use tails 'for a rudder while flying,' meaning to steer.

questions.q: Where did Tip sprinkle most of the powder?
options: On the wings, as the Tin Woodman advised
questions.why: Nick advised putting 'most on the wings,' and Tip then did the wings, sofas, and broom.

questions.q: When there was little powder left, why did the Scarecrow decide it should go on the head rather than the legs?
options: The head was the lightest part
Everything needs a head to direct it, and a flying creature does not need living legs
questions.why: He says everything 'must have a head to direct it,' and since it will fly, the legs don't matter.

questions.q: How did Tip know how to bring the Thing to life?
options: Glinda taught him in a dream
He had heard Mombi's magic words and had already used them on the Sawhorse
He read them on the pepper-box
The Woggle-Bug learned them in school
questions.why: Tip remembered Mombi's words and gestures and had successfully animated the Sawhorse before.

questions.q: What happened right after Tip spoke the magic words?
options: The Thing shuddered, the Gump screeched, and the wings flopped furiously
questions.why: The Thing shuddered, the Gump made its screeching cry, and the wings began 'flopping furiously.'

questions.q: Who nearly blew away because he was so light, and who saved him?
options: The Scarecrow; Tip caught his leg
The Woggle-Bug; Jack caught his arm
Jack; the Tin Woodman held him
questions.why: The lightweight Scarecrow became airborne until Tip caught his leg.

questions.q: How did the decision to bring the Gump's head to life prove wise?
options: The head scared away Jinjur's army
The head let the Gump walk down the stairs
The Gump heard Tip's command, turned its head, and flew back to the roof
questions.why: Because the head was alive, the Gump could respond to 'Come back!' and return to the roof.

questions.q: What is surprising about the Gump's voice?
options: It is squeaky, even though its body is enormous
questions.why: The Gump speaks in a squeaky voice despite its huge body.

questions.q: What is the last thing the Gump clearly remembers from its earlier life?
options: Walking through the forest and hearing a loud noise
questions.why: It says 'The last thing I remember distinctly is walking through the forest and hearing a loud noise.'

questions.q: What worry does the Gump express about serving the group?
options: It does not like the Woggle-Bug
It is not likely to live long in a state of slavery
It wants to return to the forest right away
questions.why: It laments 'I am not likely to live long in a state of slavery,' which touches the Tin Woodman.

questions.q: How does the Tin Woodman react to the Gump's sad words?
options: He threatens the Gump with his axe
He is moved emotionally, showing his tender heart
questions.why: The Tin Woodman responds emotionally to the Gump's sad statement.

questions.q: Where do the travelers decide to fly, and why?
options: South to Glinda the Good, to ask her advice
North to find Mombi and defeat her
East to the Field Mouse village for help
Back to the schoolhouse of Professor Nowitall
questions.why: They decide on Glinda: 'Let us go to her and ask her advice.'

questions.q: When each companion brags about himself, what does Jack Pumpkinhead mention?
questions.why: Jack notes his unchanging smile, while others boast of brains, heart, and education.

questions.q: Why does Tip scold the Woggle-Bug during the flight?
options: For making an unfeeling pun about Jack's head becoming squash
For steering the Gump the wrong way
questions.why: The Woggle-Bug punned about heads becoming squash, and Tip scolded him for the unfeeling joke.

questions.q: What did Tip do with the pepper-box before its secret was discovered?
options: He cast it aside, thinking it was useless
He threw it at the Jackdaws
He used it to steer the Gump
questions.why: Tip cast the empty pepper-box aside before the Tin Woodman examined it more closely.

questions.q: What did the Tin Woodman notice about the pepper-box?
options: It had a hole in the lid
It had Mombi's name on it
questions.why: He saw that the inside bottom was 'fully an inch away' from the outside bottom, and Tip unscrewed it.

questions.q: What was hidden inside the pepper-box's false bottom?
options: Three silver pills and a folded paper of directions
questions.why: Tip found 'three silver pills, with a carefully folded paper lying underneath them.'

questions.q: Whose pills were they, according to the paper?
questions.why: The paper was labeled 'Dr. Nikidik's Celebrated Wishing Pills.'

questions.q: What were the directions for using a Wishing Pill?
options: Swallow one pill, count seventeen by twos, then make a wish
Crush the pill, sprinkle it, and say three words
Swallow all three pills at once
Hold the pill and spin around seven times
questions.why: The paper read: 'Swallow one pill; count seventeen by twos; then make a Wish.'

questions.q: Why did the pills seem useless at first?
options: The pills had turned to dust
Seventeen is an odd number, so it can't be reached by counting by twos
The paper was written in a strange language
questions.why: The Scarecrow notes that seventeen is odd, so counting to it by twos seems impossible.

questions.q: What did Jack want to wish for?
options: That he had two legs again
That his head would never spoil
questions.why: Jack was disappointed because he wanted to wish his head would never spoil.

questions.q: What did the travelers see at dawn that showed they were no longer in Oz?
options: Rolling plains with strange villages and unfamiliar houses and animals
The green towers of the Emerald City
questions.why: They saw 'rolling plains dotted with queer villages,' and the Scarecrow said they had left Oz.

questions.q: How did the Gump crash?
options: It ran out of powder and fell asleep
It missed a rocky ledge and broke off both its right wings
It flew into a tree during a storm
questions.why: It 'missed it by half the width of his body, breaking off both his right wings against the sharp edge of the rock.'

questions.q: Why were the travelers not badly hurt when they fell?
options: They landed in a deep lake
The Gump carried them gently down
They landed in a huge Jackdaw nest full of soft leaves, papers, and straw
questions.why: The nest's soft materials cushioned their fall.

questions.q: Why were the travelers trapped in the nest?
options: Below was a steep drop of hundreds of feet, and above was a smooth cliff
A magic spell held them there
The Gump was blocking the only door
questions.why: Below lay a sheer precipice and above only smooth cliff.

questions.q: Why did the nest contain a diamond necklace and many other small objects?
options: The Woggle-Bug had hidden his treasures there
The Gump brought them from the palace
Thieving Jackdaws had collected stolen items there over many years
questions.why: The nest was filled with articles the Jackdaws had stolen over many years; the Woggle-Bug gave the necklace to the Tin Woodman.

questions.q: How did the Scarecrow try to protect Tip and the Woggle-Bug before the Jackdaws arrived?
options: He told them to jump off the ledge
He blew the silver whistle for the mice
He had Nick take him apart and scatter his straw over them to hide them
He used a Wishing Pill to make them invisible
questions.why: The Tin Woodman took the Scarecrow apart and 'scattered the straw over Tip and the Woggle-Bug, completely covering their bodies.'

questions.q: When the Jackdaws attack, how does the Tin Woodman defend himself?
options: He whirls his axe swiftly around his head
He hides beneath the Gump's body
He throws handfuls of straw at the birds
He shouts until the birds grow frightened
questions.why: The text says the Woodman picked up his axe and made it whirl swiftly around his head.

questions.q: The narrator says the Tin Woodman could fight 'as fiercely as a Roman gladiator.' What does this comparison suggest?
options: He was trained as a soldier in Rome
He enjoyed fighting more than anything else
Though usually peaceful, he could fight hard when he had to
He was too weak to fight well
questions.why: The chapter says he was usually a peaceful man but could fight fiercely when the occasion required.

questions.q: How does the Sawhorse help fight the Jackdaws?
options: It bites them with its wooden teeth
It kicks at them with its wooden legs
questions.why: The Sawhorse fights by kicking at the birds with its wooden legs.

questions.q: What do the Jackdaws do to the Scarecrow?
options: They carry him away to another nest
They peck holes in his painted face
They steal his clothing and boots
They pull out all his straw and fling it into the chasm below
questions.why: The Jackdaws stole his straw to the last wisp and flung it into the chasm beneath the nest.

questions.q: What finally makes the Jackdaws flee?
options: Tip sprinkles them with the Powder of Life
The Woggle-Bug makes a long speech
A storm blows across the mountains
The Gump frees itself from a rock peg and flops into the nest
questions.why: When the Gump freed itself and sank flopping into the nest, the birds were alarmed and fled screaming over the mountains.

questions.q: The chasm below the nest is described as one that 'yawned for hundreds of feet.' In this context, 'yawned' means the chasm was:
questions.why: A chasm that 'yawned for hundreds of feet' is a huge, deep opening, not a sleepy one.

questions.q: After the fight, what is left of the Scarecrow?
options: His clothing, with his head and brains still safe
His straw, but not his clothes
questions.why: The Woggle-Bug points out that the Scarecrow's clothing is still safe, and the Scarecrow says his brains are the same old material.

questions.q: What does Tip discover in the bottom of the Jackdaws' nest?
options: A second box of Powder of Life
Thousands of paper bills of many amounts
Fresh straw from a farmer's field
questions.why: Tip finds dollar bills, two-dollar bills, fives, tens, twenties and fifties in the bottom of the nest.

questions.q: Why were so many bills in the nest?
options: The Jackdaws had collected stolen things over many years
The Scarecrow had hidden his fortune there
Glinda had left them as a reward
Jinjur's army had thrown them away
questions.why: The nest held treasure the Jackdaws had stolen and gathered over time.

questions.q: How do the friends solve the problem of the Scarecrow's missing straw?
options: They stuff him with Jackdaw feathers
They use grass from the mountainside
They stuff him with the paper money
They leave him empty until they reach home
questions.why: With no straw available, they fill the Scarecrow's clothes with the bills from the nest.

questions.q: Which part of the Scarecrow is filled with five-dollar bills?
questions.why: The text says his left leg and boot were stuffed with five-dollar bills, while his right leg got tens.

questions.q: After being stuffed, the Scarecrow jokes that he might be mistaken for a 'Safety Deposit Vault.' What does he mean?
options: He feels locked up and trapped
He is too heavy to walk
He wants to keep his brains in a box
He is now full of valuable money, like a bank's safe
questions.why: A safety deposit vault stores valuables, and the Scarecrow is now stuffed with bills, so he says he feels like a new man.

questions.q: Where does the Scarecrow keep the box of Wishing Pills?
options: In a knapsack on the Sawhorse
questions.why: The Scarecrow takes the box from his jacket pocket.

questions.q: What is the puzzling rule for making a Wishing Pill work?
options: You must say the wish backward
You must count seventeen by twos
You must swallow all the pills at once
You must stand on one foot at sunset
questions.why: The pills require counting seventeen by twos, which seems impossible when counting normally.

questions.q: Who surprises everyone by solving the counting puzzle?
questions.why: The Sawhorse abruptly asks, 'Why not start counting at a half of one?'

questions.q: Why does the Sawhorse's idea work?
options: Starting at one-half, counting by twos reaches seventeen
Counting slowly makes any number work
questions.why: Counting one-half, one, three, five, and so on by twos lands exactly on seventeen.

questions.q: What happens right after Tip swallows the first pill and counts?
options: He feels a terrible pain and thinks he has been poisoned
He instantly flies into the air
He falls asleep for a whole day
questions.why: Tip gasps, 'The pill has poisoned me!'

questions.q: What does Tip wish for while in pain, and what is the result?
options: That the pain would stop, and he becomes stronger
That he were home, and he lands in Gillikin Country
That he had never swallowed the pill, and all three pills are back in the box
That the Jackdaws would return, and they do
questions.why: Tip wishes he'd never swallowed the pill, and then the Scarecrow finds all three pills in the box again.

questions.q: What does the Woggle-Bug wish for?
options: That the Scarecrow be stuffed with fresh straw
That the Gump's broken wings be mended and as good as new
That they all return to the Emerald City
That he become the wisest creature in Oz
questions.why: The Woggle-Bug says, 'I wish the Gump's broken wings mended, and as good as new!'

questions.q: Which lesson does Tip's first wish best show?
options: Wishes should always be made for money
It is best to let the Sawhorse make every choice
A wish made carelessly in a moment of panic can be wasted
questions.why: Tip's panicked wish only undid his own swallowing, so nothing useful was gained until the Woggle-Bug wished carefully.

chapters.title: 20. The Scarecrow Appeals to Glinda the Good

questions.q: Why do the travelers wait before leaving the Jackdaws' nest?
options: They are waiting for Glinda to arrive
They decide to wait until morning
questions.why: The group decides to wait until morning to leave.

questions.q: Which treasure does Tip take from the nest?
questions.why: While searching the nest, Tip takes a gold watch.

questions.q: Which friend adorns himself with rings from the nest?
questions.why: The Scarecrow puts on rings, while the Woggle-Bug takes bracelets and Jack gets jeweled brooches.

questions.q: What makes the adventurers hurry aboard the Gump in the morning?
options: The nest begins to fall apart
A great flock of Jackdaws comes to fight again
A storm blows in from the desert
questions.why: A great flock of Jackdaws approached for one more battle, so the adventurers boarded the Gump quickly.

questions.q: How do the travelers realize they are in Munchkin territory?
options: A sign on the road tells them
questions.why: Blue houses tell them they are over the Munchkins' country.

questions.q: What unpleasant discovery does the Scarecrow make during the flight?
options: All his paper money has blown away
The pepper-box with the two remaining Wishing Pills is gone
questions.why: When the Scarecrow searches his pocket for the pepper-box containing the two silver Wishing Pills, it cannot be found.

questions.q: How do the travelers know they have reached the domain of Glinda the Good?
options: They see Glinda waving from a tower
questions.why: The text shows the party noticing that everything is red in Glinda's country.

questions.q: Where does the Gump land?
options: On the roof of Glinda's palace
In the middle of a red desert
On a velvety green lawn by a fountain in Glinda's gardens
questions.why: It settles on a velvety green lawn close by a fountain in Glinda's gardens.

questions.q: Who are the soldiers who meet the travelers at Glinda's palace?
options: Girls in neat uniforms carrying swords and spears
questions.why: Glinda's soldiers are girls in neat uniforms bearing swords and spears.

questions.q: Why does the Captain of the guard greet the visitors respectfully?
options: She mistakes Tip for a prince
She recognizes the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman
She is afraid of the Gump
Glinda has told her to bow to everyone
questions.why: The Captain recognizes the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow report to Glinda about Queen Jinjur's rule?
options: Her army has enslaved the men and robbed the city of its emeralds
She has made the Emerald City rich and peaceful
She has invited Glinda to a feast
She has returned the throne to the Scarecrow
questions.why: The Scarecrow says Jinjur's forces enslaved the men and robbed the streets and buildings of their emerald jewels.

questions.q: How does Glinda respond when the Scarecrow tells her the news?
options: She says she already knows all about it
She asks the Gump to repeat it
questions.why: Glinda tells them she already knows, and the Scarecrow says nothing in Oz escapes her notice.

questions.q: According to Glinda, from whom did the Wizard take the throne?
options: The Wicked Witch of the West
questions.why: Glinda says the Wizard took the throne from Pastoria, the former King.

questions.q: How does the Scarecrow defend his own right to rule?
options: The Wizard gave him the crown fairly
Pastoria is dead, and someone must rule in his place
He has the best brains in Oz
questions.why: The Scarecrow replies that Pastoria is dead and gone and someone must rule in his place.

questions.q: What important secret does Glinda share about Pastoria?
options: He is still alive in the desert
He had a daughter, Ozma, who is the rightful heir
He was really the Wizard in disguise
questions.why: Glinda says Pastoria had a daughter, Ozma, who is the rightful heir to the throne of the Emerald City.

questions.q: How does Glinda search for clues about the Wizard?
options: She flies over the Emerald City
She asks Jinjur to send a letter
She reads a book in her library that records the Wizard's actions in Oz
questions.why: Glinda says she will carefully read, that night, the book that records every action of the Wizard while he was in Oz.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the Wizard's actions that Glinda finds in the records?
options: He built a hot-air balloon for Jinjur
He hid the Powder of Life in the palace
He traveled to Glinda's castle twice
He made three secret visits to old Mombi
questions.why: The records show he ate beans with a knife, made three secret visits to Mombi, and limped slightly on his left foot.

questions.q: Why does Glinda believe Mombi helped hide Ozma?
options: Mombi wrote Glinda a letter admitting it
The Wizard visited Mombi secretly and likely taught her magic
Tip told Glinda he had seen a princess
questions.why: Glinda reasons the Wizard taught Mombi his magic tricks, so Mombi must have helped him hide the girl.

questions.q: Glinda's reasoning from the three odd facts in the records is most like the work of a:
options: detective finding the one clue that matters
questions.why: Of the three facts (beans, visits, limp), Glinda picks the visits to Mombi as the meaningful clue and draws a conclusion from it.

questions.q: What does Glinda decide to do at the end of the chapter?
options: Make the Scarecrow King again right away
March her army to the Emerald City at daybreak and capture Mombi
questions.why: Glinda declares she will march with her army to the Emerald City at daybreak and take Mombi prisoner.

chapters.title: 21. The Tin Woodman Plucks a Rose

questions.q: When does Glinda's army assemble to begin its march?
questions.why: The army assembles at dawn, as Glinda planned the day before.

questions.q: What weapons do the girl soldiers carry?
questions.why: The girl soldiers carry silver-tipped spears.

questions.q: What are the officers' shields edged with?
questions.why: The officers carry sharp swords and shields edged with peacock feathers.

questions.q: How does Glinda travel with her army?
options: Walking at the front of the army
In a beautiful palanquin carried by twelve servants
questions.why: Glinda rides in a palanquin borne by twelve servants.

questions.q: A 'palanquin' is best described as:
options: a covered chair or bed carried on poles by people
questions.why: The palanquin is carried by twelve servants, which shows it is a seat carried by people.

questions.q: When does the army reach the walls of the Emerald City?
questions.why: The party reaches the city walls after nightfall and pitches tents.

questions.q: How is Glinda's own tent different from her soldiers' tents?
options: Hers is pure white silk with scarlet banners, while theirs are scarlet silk
Hers is green, while theirs are blue
Hers is made of tin, while theirs are cloth
Hers is the smallest tent of all
questions.why: The soldiers pitch tents of scarlet silk, while Glinda's tent is pure white silk with scarlet banners.

questions.q: What does Jinjur exclaim when she sees the army from a palace tower?
questions.why: Jinjur despairs, 'We are surely lost!'

questions.q: What does Glinda demand from Jinjur?
options: That she hand over old Mombi as a prisoner
That she give the throne to the Scarecrow at once
That she pay a bag of emeralds
questions.why: Glinda says Jinjur must deliver up old Mombi to be her prisoner.

questions.q: How does Mombi try to trick Glinda?
options: She makes Jellia Jamb look like Mombi and sends her to Glinda
She pretends to be Glinda's Captain
questions.why: Mombi uses magic to give Jellia Jamb her own appearance, and the disguised Jellia is sent to Glinda.

questions.q: Why does Glinda become suspicious of the 'Mombi' she is given?
options: The prisoner knows nothing about Ozma and begins to weep
The prisoner laughs at the Scarecrow
questions.why: Jellia knew nothing of Ozma and grew so nervous under questioning that she began to weep, to Glinda's astonishment.

questions.q: How does Glinda return Jellia to her own shape?
options: By sprinkling the Powder of Life
By saying a few potent words and making a peculiar gesture
questions.why: Glinda utters a few potent words and makes a peculiar gesture to transform the girl back.

questions.q: Who cries out, "Why, it's Jellia Jamb!"?
questions.why: The Scarecrow recognizes her and says, 'Why, it's Jellia Jamb!'

questions.q: What does Jellia ask of Glinda after telling about Mombi's trick?
options: To be sent back to Jinjur
Her protection, which Glinda readily grants
To join Glinda's army as captain
To be turned back into Mombi
questions.why: Jellia begs Glinda's protection, and the Sorceress readily grants it.

questions.q: What terms does Jinjur's messenger offer Glinda?
options: Glinda may search the city, but must leave peaceably if Mombi isn't found by sundown
Glinda may rule the city for one day
Jinjur will surrender if Glinda gives her the Gump
Glinda must fight Jinjur alone at noon
questions.why: Jinjur says Glinda is welcome to search, but if Mombi isn't found by sundown she must go away and bother them no more.

questions.q: How does Glinda enter the Emerald City?
options: Her soldiers climb over the walls at night
She flies over the walls on the Gump
Jinjur opens the gates and Glinda marches in with a company of soldiers
She digs a tunnel under the gate
questions.why: Glinda agrees to the terms, and Jinjur has the gates thrown open.

questions.q: What form does Mombi take to avoid being found?
options: A red rose growing on a bush in the palace garden
A green emerald in the palace wall
A black cat in the kitchen
A statue in the throne room
questions.why: The witch transforms herself into a red rose growing on a bush in the palace garden.

questions.q: Why does the Tin Woodman pick the red rose?
options: He needs it for a magic spell
questions.why: The text says the Tin Woodman, who was fond of flowers, spied the big red rose and plucked it.

questions.q: What is ironic about the Tin Woodman picking the rose?
options: He has no nose to smell it
He carries the very witch they are hunting without knowing it
Roses do not grow in the Emerald City
questions.why: Mombi is the rose, so the searchers unknowingly carry her away in his buttonhole.

questions.q: How does Glinda feel at the end of the search?
options: She is sure Mombi is in the garden
She is glad to go home
She believes she has been defeated by the witch's cunning
questions.why: After hours of vain searching, Glinda realizes she has been defeated by the superior cunning of the aged witch.

questions.q: How does Mombi feel when she first finds herself in the Tin Woodman's buttonhole?
options: Angry, so she bites the Woodman
Happy, because she wants to be caught
Sleepy, so she takes a nap
Frightened at first, then sure she is just as safe there
questions.why: The witch is at first frightened but decides she is as safe in the buttonhole as on the bush.

questions.q: What does Glinda say about the expedition at the start of the council?
options: It has been a great success
Since they failed to find Mombi, it may prove a failure
They should attack Jinjur at once
questions.why: Glinda says they have failed to find cunning old Mombi, so she fears the expedition will fail.

questions.q: Why does Glinda say she cannot simply attack Jinjur?
options: She has promised not to molest Jinjur
The Scarecrow asked her not to
questions.why: Glinda states, 'But I have promised not to molest Jinjur.'

questions.q: What makes Glinda suspect the rose is Mombi?
options: She thinks she sees its big red leaves tremble slightly
questions.why: Glinda noticed the rose in the Woodman's buttonhole and imagined she saw its leaves tremble slightly.

questions.q: What is Mombi's first transformation after she is discovered?
options: A Shadow gliding along the wall
questions.why: Mombi immediately takes the form of a Shadow and glides along the wall.

questions.q: How does Glinda stop the Shadow from escaping?
options: She lights every lamp in the tent
She tells the Gump to block the door
She reaches the tent opening first and closes it with a wave of her hand
She throws her golden thread over it
questions.why: Glinda closes the entrance so securely with a wave of her hand that Mombi can't find a crack to creep through.

questions.q: Into what does Mombi transform after the Shadow?
questions.why: Mombi changes from a shadow to a Black Ant.

questions.q: Why might Mombi have chosen to become a Shadow and then an Ant?
options: Both are hard to catch and could slip through small spaces
questions.why: Mombi looks for a crack to creep through as a Shadow and then seeks hiding places as a tiny Ant.

questions.q: When does Mombi make her last transformation?
options: When the Scarecrow opens the tent
Just as Glinda's hand is coming down to catch the Ant
questions.why: Just as Glinda's hand was descending, the frantic witch made her last transformation.

questions.q: What is Mombi's final form in this chase?
questions.why: Mombi becomes a huge Griffin and springs through the tent wall.

questions.q: How does the Griffin get out of the tent?
options: It springs through the wall, tearing the silk
It flies out through the roof hole
It walks out the open door
questions.why: The Griffin sprang through the wall of the tent, tearing the silk asunder.

questions.q: The Griffin 'darted away with the speed of a whirlwind.' This phrase shows the Griffin was:
questions.why: A whirlwind is a fast, powerful wind, so the comparison shows great speed.

questions.q: How does Glinda chase the Griffin?
questions.why: Glinda pursues Mombi on the Sawhorse.

questions.q: How does the author describe the Sawhorse's legs during the chase?
options: They creaked like an old door
They moved so fast they twinkled like the rays of a star
questions.why: The Sawhorse's legs moved so fast that they twinkled like the rays of a star.

questions.q: How do Tip and the other friends follow the chase?
options: They ride on Glinda's soldiers' shoulders
They stay behind in the tent
questions.why: The friends run to where the Gump is lying and quickly tumble aboard.

questions.q: Why does the Griffin finally collapse?
options: Glinda hits it with a spear
It runs into the Emerald City wall
Its tired feet sink into the desert sand and it becomes exhausted
questions.why: In the desert, the Griffin's tired feet sank far into the sand and it fell forward, completely exhausted.

questions.q: What does Glinda use to capture Mombi?
options: A slender golden thread from her girdle
questions.why: Glinda unwinds a slender golden thread from her girdle and throws it over the Griffin's head.

questions.q: What happens when the golden thread falls over the Griffin's head?
options: It makes the Griffin fly away
It destroys the magic of Mombi's transformation
It turns Mombi into a rose again
questions.why: The thread destroys the magical power of Mombi's transformation, and the old Witch appears.

questions.q: How does Mombi look at Glinda at the end of the chapter?
questions.why: The old Witch is left glaring savagely at the serene and beautiful face of the Sorceress.

questions.q: Which idea does this chapter show most clearly?
options: Patience and sharp watching can beat trickery
Friends should never help one another
questions.why: Glinda's close watching of the trembling rose and her steady pursuit defeat each of Mombi's clever disguises.

questions.q: Why can't Mombi escape while in Glinda's camp?
options: She is helpless while the magic golden thread is around her throat
She is locked in an iron cage
She is too tired to move
questions.why: The old hag is helpless so long as the magical thread encircles her throat.

questions.q: What two things does Glinda want Mombi to explain?
options: Where the Powder of Life came from and who made the Gump
Why Jinjur rebelled and where the emeralds are
Why the Wizard visited her three times and what happened to Ozma
How to make Wishing Pills and where the Jackdaws live
questions.why: Glinda asks about the Wizard's three visits and the vanished Princess Ozma.

questions.q: What does Glinda say will happen if Mombi refuses to tell what she knows?
options: Glinda will send her to Kansas
Glinda will put her to death
Glinda will turn her into a rose
Glinda will let her go free
questions.why: Glinda says, unless you tell me all that you know, I will certainly put you to death.

questions.q: If Mombi tells the truth, what will Glinda make her do?
options: Drink a draught that makes her forget all her magic
questions.why: Glinda offers to have Mombi drink a powerful draught causing her to forget all the magic she has learned.

questions.q: How does Glinda's magic pearl work?
options: It glows red when someone is afraid
It grants one wish a day
It stays pure white only when the truth is spoken
questions.why: Glinda says the pearl will remain pure white only when the truth is spoken.

questions.q: What lie does Mombi first tell about the Wizard's visits?
options: That he came to buy her farm
That he came to learn how she makes tea-biscuits
That he never visited at all
That he came to borrow her broom
questions.why: Mombi claims he visited to learn how she makes tea-biscuits, and the pearl turns black.

questions.q: What does the pearl turning black prove?
questions.why: Glinda declares, 'Then you have told me a falsehood!'

questions.q: According to Mombi, what did the Wizard bring her?
options: The girl Ozma, then only a baby, to hide
questions.why: Mombi admits the Wizard brought her the baby Ozma and begged her to conceal the child.

questions.q: What did the Wizard give Mombi in return for hiding Ozma?
options: He taught her all the magic tricks he knew
He gave her a bag of gold
He made her Queen of the Gillikins
questions.why: Mombi says the Wizard taught her all his tricks, some good and some only frauds.

questions.q: How did Mombi hide Princess Ozma?
options: She locked her in a tower
She sent her across the desert
She transformed her into a boy, Tip
She turned her into a rose
questions.why: Mombi confesses she changed the princess into a boy, and that boy is Tip.

questions.q: How does Tip first react to the news?
options: He is pleased and asks for a crown
He is amazed and says he is no Princess Ozma
He laughs and thinks it's a joke
He runs away into the desert
questions.why: Tip cries in amazement, 'Why, I'm no Princess Ozma—I'm not a girl!'

questions.q: What would Tip rather do instead of ruling?
options: Go back to live with Mombi
Let Jinjur be Queen while he travels with the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman
questions.why: Tip pleads to let Jinjur be Queen so he can stay a boy and travel with his friends.

questions.q: What does the Tin Woodman promise Tip?
options: He will give Tip his tin castle
He will make Tip a tin crown
They will all remain faithful friends just the same
questions.why: The Tin Woodman says it doesn't hurt to be a girl and they will remain faithful friends.

questions.q: What does the Woggle-Bug offer to do?
questions.why: The Woggle-Bug says girls are equally good students and he would like to become her tutor.

questions.q: Why is Jack Pumpkinhead worried about Tip's change?
options: If Tip becomes a girl, Tip can't be his 'dear father' anymore
He thinks his pumpkin head will spoil
He wants to be King himself
questions.why: Jack gasps that if Tip becomes a girl, he can't be Jack's dear father anymore.

questions.q: On what condition does Tip first agree to try the change?
options: That he may keep the Gump
That he be changed back into a boy if he doesn't like it
questions.why: Tip says he might try it for a while, but if he doesn't like it they must promise to change him back.

questions.q: Why does Glinda ask Mombi, not herself, to do the transformation?
options: Glinda does not practice transformations, which only unscrupulous witches use
Glinda is too tired after the chase
Mombi is more powerful than Glinda
questions.why: Glinda says it is beyond her magic, since only unscrupulous witches use that art.

questions.q: What does Tip generously promise about Mombi?
options: To make her his royal advisor
To send her back to her farm with gold
To provide for her in her old age if he becomes ruler
To give her the Powder of Life
questions.why: Tip promises to provide for Mombi in her old age if he becomes ruler of the Emerald City.

questions.q: How does Mombi's spell begin?
options: Tip drinks a potion that puts him in a deep, dreamless sleep
Tip counts to seventeen by twos
questions.why: Tip drinks a potion that quickly sends him into a deep and dreamless sleep before Mombi works her magic.

questions.q: After Ozma says she is "just the same Tip... only—only—", Jack adds, "Only you're different!" Why does the narrator call this Jack's wisest speech?
options: It is the longest speech Jack ever gives
It shows Jack is secretly a wizard
It honestly admits a real change while the friendship stays the same
questions.why: The narrator calls Jack's short reply the wisest speech he ever made, since Ozma is still their friend but has truly changed.

questions.q: What news reaches Queen Jinjur at the start of the chapter?
options: The Scarecrow wants to marry her
Mombi was captured and confessed, and Princess Ozma was found
questions.why: Jinjur learns that Mombi was captured, confessed to Glinda, and that the long-lost Ozma was discovered.

questions.q: What does Jinjur dread going back to?
questions.why: Jinjur complains she must go back to scrubbing floors and churning butter after ruling as Queen.

questions.q: Why does Jinjur send a sharp defiance instead of surrendering?
options: Her soldiers counsel her to resist, and she listens
She thinks the Gump is broken
questions.why: Her soldiers counseled resistance, and she listened to their foolish prattle and sent a sharp defiance.

questions.q: The narrator calls the soldiers' advice 'foolish prattle.' 'Prattle' means:
questions.why: Calling the advice foolish prattle shows it was silly chatter, not wise counsel.

questions.q: How does Glinda's army look as it marches on the city?
options: Pennants flying, bands playing, and a forest of shining spears
Silent and hidden in the dark
questions.why: The army marches with pennants flying, bands playing, and a forest of shining spears.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow suggest to get past the city walls?
options: Use the Gump, which can still fly
Wait for Jinjur to get hungry
questions.why: The Scarecrow says, 'We still have the Gump, and the Gump can still fly.'

questions.q: What is Jinjur doing when the flying party finds her?
options: Reclining in a hammock, reading a novel and eating green chocolates
questions.why: Jinjur is in a hammock reading a green-covered novel and eating green chocolates.

questions.q: What does Jinjur's activity suggest about her as a ruler?
options: She was working hard to defend the city
She was preparing a clever attack
She cared more about her own comfort than about ruling well
questions.why: While an army stood outside her walls, Jinjur was lounging in a hammock with a novel and chocolates.

questions.q: What happens to Jinjur after her capture?
options: She is banished across the desert
She is made Ozma's chief general
She is turned into a statue
She is chained, then released on a promise of good behavior
questions.why: Jinjur is locked in chains and later released on promise of good behavior.

questions.q: What is Ozma's first act as ruler?
options: Making the Army of Revolt return every stolen emerald and gem
questions.why: Ozma's first act was to oblige the Army of Revolt to return every stolen emerald or gem.

questions.q: How is peace restored in the families of the Emerald City?
options: The men cast off their aprons and the women cook a delicious feast
Glinda casts a spell on every home
questions.why: The men cast off their aprons, and the women prepared a feast that immediately restored harmony.

questions.q: What does the Gump ask for?
options: To fly back to the Jackdaws
To be given a new body
questions.why: The Gump says, 'Please take me to pieces,' and begs to be dispersed.

questions.q: Why does the Gump want this?
options: It never wished to be brought to life and is ashamed of its patched-together self
It wants to rest on a mantelpiece forever
It is afraid of Glinda's soldiers
questions.why: The Gump says it did not wish to be brought to life and is ashamed of its 'conglomerate personality.'

questions.q: The Gump calls itself a 'conglomerate personality.' 'Conglomerate' here means:
options: made of many different parts put together
questions.why: The Gump was built from sofas, palm leaves, a broom, and a head, so it is made of many parts.

questions.q: What happens to the Gump's head afterward?
options: It is buried in the garden
It hangs over a mantelpiece and still talks now and then
It is given to the Jackdaws
It becomes the Sawhorse's new head
questions.why: The antlered head hangs over a mantelpiece and occasionally speaks.

questions.q: What new job does the Woggle-Bug receive?
questions.why: The Woggle-Bug is appointed to the important post of Public Educator.

questions.q: What does Ozma do for the Sawhorse?
options: Has its wooden legs shod with gold so they won't wear out
questions.why: Ozma has its wooden legs shod with gold, and the tinkle of the shoes fills her subjects with awe.

questions.q: Why does the Tin Woodman joke that the Scarecrow is a good Royal Treasurer?
options: The Scarecrow is made of money
The Scarecrow can count to seventeen by twos
The Scarecrow once guarded the Jackdaws' nest
questions.why: The Tin Woodman says it is a good thing to have a Royal Treasurer who is made of money.

questions.q: What does the Scarecrow say about brains and money?
options: Brains are far superior to money in every way
Money is more useful than brains
Brains and money are useless in Oz
He would trade his brains for gold
questions.why: The Scarecrow says, 'I consider brains far superior to money, in every way.'

questions.q: What does Ozma mean when she calls her friends rich in 'the riches of content'?
options: They own the most emeralds in Oz
They will soon find more treasure
Being satisfied with what you have is the only riches worth having
questions.why: After the Scarecrow praises brains and the Tin Woodman praises a good heart, Ozma says their contentment is the only riches worth having.

verdicts.high: Highly Magnified and Thoroughly Educated — superb reading!
verdicts.pass: Well done. On to the next chapter.
verdicts.fail: Below the passing mark. Read it again and come back.

questions.q: At the start of the novel, who is Tip's guardian?
questions.why: Tip lives with Mombi in the Gillikin Country at the book's opening.

questions.q: In which part of Oz does Tip's story begin?
options: The Quadling Country in the south
The Gillikin Country in the north
The Winkie Country in the west
questions.why: Tip grows up with Mombi in the Gillikin Country.

questions.q: Why does Tip make Jack Pumpkinhead in the first place?
options: To frighten Mombi as a prank
To keep him company on a long trip
questions.why: Tip builds the pumpkin-headed man as a prank to scare Mombi.

questions.q: What magical substance brings Jack, the Sawhorse, and the Gump to life?
questions.why: The Powder of Life animates each of these characters.

questions.q: What does Mombi threaten to do to Tip that makes him run away?
options: Send him to the Emerald City
Turn him into a marble statue
questions.why: Mombi's threat to transform Tip into marble drives him to flee with Jack.

questions.q: Who leads the Army of Revolt that conquers the Emerald City?
questions.why: General Jinjur leads the army of girls that overthrows the Scarecrow.

questions.q: Who is ruling the Emerald City when Tip first arrives there?
questions.why: The Scarecrow has ruled since the Wizard left.

questions.q: What creature, 'Highly Magnified and Thoroughly Educated,' joins Tip's group?
questions.why: The Woggle-Bug calls himself Highly Magnified and Thoroughly Educated.

questions.q: Where do the friends go to plan how to take back the Emerald City before seeking Glinda?
options: The Tin Woodman's castle in the Winkie Country
questions.why: The group escapes to the Tin Woodman's castle in the Winkie Country to plan.

questions.q: What is the Gump built from?
options: Tin plates and an oil can
Two sofas, palm-leaf wings, a broom tail, and an antlered head
questions.why: The friends build the flying Gump from sofas, palm leaves, a broom and a mounted head, and later take it apart into those pieces.

questions.q: Why does the Gump end up in the Jackdaws' nest?
options: It flies off course and crashes, breaking a wing
The friends go there to hunt treasure
questions.why: The flying machine goes astray and lands broken in the Jackdaws' nest.

questions.q: How is the Scarecrow's problem of lost straw solved in the nest?
options: He is stuffed with paper money
questions.why: The friends fill the Scarecrow with bills found in the nest.

questions.q: Who reveals that the rightful ruler of the Emerald City is Pastoria's daughter, Ozma?
questions.why: Glinda tells the Scarecrow that Pastoria's daughter Ozma is the rightful heir.

questions.q: How had the Wizard kept Ozma from the throne?
options: He gave the baby to Mombi to hide
He turned her into a Jackdaw
He locked her in the palace
questions.why: Mombi confesses the Wizard brought her the baby Ozma to conceal, and she changed her into a boy.

questions.q: What surprising secret about Tip is revealed near the end?
options: Tip is really Princess Ozma under Mombi's spell
questions.why: Mombi reveals she transformed Princess Ozma into the boy Tip.

questions.q: Which disguise does Mombi use to hide from Glinda in the Emerald City?
questions.why: Mombi becomes a red rose in the palace garden, which the Tin Woodman picks.

questions.q: What shape does Mombi take when she tries to flee from Glinda across the desert?
questions.why: Mombi turns herself into a Griffin to outrun Glinda, but Glinda pursues and captures her before she can escape.

questions.q: Who rules the Emerald City at the end of the novel?
questions.why: Ozma is crowned and rules her people with wisdom and justice.

questions.q: Where do the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman go at the end?
options: To the Winkie Country, with the Scarecrow as Royal Treasurer
To Glinda's palace to be soldiers
questions.why: The Scarecrow goes home with the Tin Woodman, who makes him Royal Treasurer.

questions.q: Which character jokingly calls Tip his 'father' throughout the story?
questions.why: Because Tip made him, Jack calls Tip his father, and worries he'll lose that when Tip becomes a girl.

questions.q: What role does magic play in Mombi's actions across the book?
options: She uses it only to help others
She uses it to protect the Emerald City
She uses it selfishly: threatening Tip, hiding Ozma, and escaping in disguises
questions.why: Mombi threatens Tip, hid Ozma for the Wizard in exchange for magic tricks, and uses transformations to escape Glinda.

questions.q: How is Glinda's use of magic different from Mombi's?
options: Glinda uses magic only for tricks
Glinda uses magic honestly and refuses to practice transformations
Glinda has no magic at all
Glinda uses transformations more than Mombi
questions.why: Glinda says transformations are used only by unscrupulous witches, so she asks Mombi to undo her own spell.

questions.q: Which theme is shown by the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman's final conversation about brains, hearts, and money?
options: True wealth comes from being content with who you are
Money is the most important thing
questions.why: Ozma tells them their riches of content are the only riches worth having.

questions.q: Which theme is shown by the loyalty of Tip's friends throughout the adventure?
options: Only people who are alike can be friends
It is safest to travel alone
questions.why: The friends stick together through dangers and promise to remain faithful even when Tip becomes Ozma.

questions.q: Many characters in the novel (Jack, the Sawhorse, the Gump) are made from ordinary objects. What does this suggest about the land of Oz?
options: In Oz, magic can give life and personality to unlikely things
Everything in Oz is made of wood
questions.why: The Powder of Life brings a pumpkin-headed man, a sawhorse, and a sofa-built flying machine to life, each with its own personality.
